t: Wherever I Go, God’s Presence Never Leaves Me
v: Where could I go from your Spirit? Or where could I flee from your presence?
If I ascend up into heaven, you are there. If I make my bed in Sheol, behold, you are there!
If I take the wings of the dawn, and settle in the uttermost parts of the sea,
even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me.
If I say, “Surely the darkness will overwhelm me. The light around me will be night,”
even the darkness doesn’t hide from you, but the night shines as the day. The darkness is like light to you.
b: This psalm paints a deep picture of God’s complete presence. Whether on the heights or in the depths, in the light of morning or the dark of night, the Spirit of God never leaves us. David is not hiding from God in fear; he is marveling in reverent awe: wherever I am, God is there.

When we stand on the mountaintops of life, God is there. When we sink into darkness, loneliness, and a future we cannot see, he still does not abandon us. Even if we “settle in the uttermost parts of the sea” and try to escape it all, his hand still leads and holds us. This is a God whose authority is love; his presence is not a threat but a protection, not a judgment but a guide.

A life that belongs to God is lived in this awareness: God is not found only in the temple, and he does not draw near only when we worship. He is with us every moment, in good times and in low places. We do not have to hold our lives together by ourselves; we can be upheld by his right hand and led by him.
a: Believe in God’s presence in every circumstance
Whether in laughter or in tears, in smooth times or hard ones, God has not left you.
When you want to run away, do not flee from God; flee to him
Do not let disappointment, fear, or shame push you away. Let God’s love be your greatest security.
Learn to trust God’s guidance in the dark
His presence does not depend on feelings; it is the assurance of faith. Even when you cannot see, he sees clearly.
q: Are there times when I doubt God’s presence? In the dark or in the valley, do I still believe he is leading me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that wherever I am and whatever I am going through, You are with me. Even when I am weak and discouraged, Your hand holds me. Help me to trust You in the dark and to turn to You when I want to run away. May I walk under Your guidance all my life and grow strong through Your presence. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Don’t Merely Worship Rituals; Truly Seek the Lord’s Face
v: Listen to this word which I take up for a lamentation over you, O house of Israel:
“The virgin of Israel has fallen; She shall rise no more. She is cast down on her land; there is no one to raise her up.”
For the Lord GOD says: “The city that went out a thousand shall have a hundred left, and that which went out one hundred shall have ten left to the house of Israel.”
For the LORD says to the house of Israel: “Seek me, and you will live;
but don’t seek Bethel, nor enter into Gilgal, and don’t pass to Beersheba; for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity, and Bethel shall come to nothing.
Seek the LORD, and you will live, lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and it devour, and there be no one to quench it in Bethel.
They hate him who reproves in the gate, and they abhor him who speaks blamelessly.

Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take taxes from him of wheat, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not dwell in them. You have planted pleasant vineyards, but you shall not drink their wine.
For I know how many are your offenses, and how great are your sins— you who afflict the just, who take a bribe, and who turn away the needy in the courts.
Therefore a prudent person keeps silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good, and not evil, that you may live; and so the LORD, the God of Armies, will be with you, as you say.
b: This passage is Amos’s warning and appeal to Israel. He begins with a lament, describing a people busy with religious activity and ritual yet having lost the heart of true reverence for God. God does not want mere outward worship; he wants them to seek him and turn from sin so that they may live.

The people relied on religious sites such as Bethel, Gilgal, and Beersheba, yet had not truly repented. These places had once been signs of meeting with God, but now they had become a comfort for false piety. The people no longer accepted rebuke, hated honest words, and even used their power to oppress the poor, accept bribes, and pervert justice.

Through Amos, God stresses: “Seek me, and you will live,” and “Seek good, and not evil.” He wants his people to move from outward piety to genuine reverence, from religious ritual to a changed life. This is a life that belongs to God: letting God be King, letting his standard guide our living, and letting his heart adjust our actions.
a: Worship cannot be only outward ritual; it needs inward repentance and longing
When you go to church, sing hymns, and pray, is it out of love for God? Or just to satisfy your own feelings?
Courageously face God’s rebuke and do not reject the reminders of truth
Honest words can sting, but if they come from God, they bring a turning toward life.
Choose each day to seek good and turn from evil
Not by judging good and evil on your own, but by letting God’s word and the Holy Spirit lead you in his way.
q: Is my faith life today only about chasing spiritual feelings and forms, or am I sincerely seeking God and living out his heart?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, shine Your light on me, so that I will not be content with outward religious form but will sincerely seek Your face. Help me turn from sin and stop being self-righteous; instead, let me repent humbly and do what pleases You. May all that I do be good in Your eyes. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Your Life Grows Not by People, but by God
v: Who then is Apollos, and who is Paul, but servants through whom you believed, and each as the Lord gave to him?
I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.
So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.
Now he who plants and he who waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
For we are God’s fellow workers. You are God’s farming, God’s building.
b: The believers in Corinth had fallen into factions over spiritual leaders. Some said, “I belong to Paul,” and others, “I belong to Apollos.” They had put people at the center of their faith and lost their focus on God. In this passage Paul says it plainly: whoever preached the gospel or helped you grow is only a servant in God’s hand. The One who truly changes and grows a life is God himself.

He uses the picture of a farmer and a laborer: Paul planted and Apollos watered, but without God’s life entering in and giving the growth, all effort is in vain. This reminds us that whether we are serving others or being shepherded and taught, we must keep our eyes on God, not lean on people, and certainly not worship them.

This is what a life that belongs to God looks like: Jesus is our example, God’s word is our standard, and the Holy Spirit is our guide. Whether you are a planter or a waterer, you are only a servant working together with God. You are part of God’s field and the building he is putting up. He is the true Master who holds authority, and what he cares about is not whom you belong to, but whether you let him work.
a: Fix your eyes on God in your faith, and do not over-depend on or idolize people
Every pastor and church leader is a vessel of God, not the foundation of your faith.
In serving, know your role: you are God’s worker, not the star
Whatever you do, the point is not to make people see you, but to let people experience God.
Let God work in your life, and be willing to receive his cultivating and building
Do not resist the work of the Holy Spirit, and do not stop at outward activity; let God’s life grow within you.
q: Does my faith lean too heavily on certain people? Am I willing to let God himself plant and build in my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for using different people to lead me to know You, but I know that You alone are the true Lord of my life. Help me not to depend on people but to fix my eyes on You. Let me be an obedient field and building in Your hands, so that the good work You have begun in me will grow day by day. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Fear of God Is the Beginning of Wisdom; Heeding Instruction Brings Blessing
v: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel:
to know wisdom and instruction; to discern the words of understanding;
to receive instruction in wise dealing, in righteousness, justice, and equity;
to give prudence to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young man—
that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel;
to understand a proverb and parables, the words and riddles of the wise.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
My son, listen to your father’s instruction, and don’t forsake your mother’s teaching;
for they will be a garland to grace your head, and chains around your neck.
b: The opening of Proverbs reveals the purpose of the whole book: to help people gain wisdom, understand instruction, discern well, and live out God’s standard in everyday life. Wisdom is not just an accumulation of knowledge; it comes from God and is the ability that guides our conduct and choices.

This passage says the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord. This is not merely dreading God’s judgment, but an attitude of honor, trust, and obedience, acknowledging that he is Lord and the One on whom everything we do depends and by whom it is measured. A life that truly belongs to God does not rely on cleverness, but centers on God, takes him as the standard, and is willing to let him rule.

The passage also stresses the importance of teaching in the family. A parent’s instruction is not an outdated restraint but a precious guide in life, a handing down of wisdom. Listening to parents and respecting authority is really learning to listen to God and obey his ways. Such a life is like wearing a crown of glory and a chain of honor around the neck, receiving respect among people and delight before God.
a: Put the fear of God first in your life, as the starting point of all you do
In everything, seek God’s will first, rather than acting on your own judgment or worldly views.
Treasure the teaching of elders and spiritual forebears
Their experience and reminders are protection, not restriction; being willing to listen saves you from many detours.
Let God’s wisdom shape your daily choices and values
Don’t revere God only in spiritual matters; live out respect for him in every decision about money, relationships, time, and more.
q: Do I truly fear God and put him first in my life? Am I willing to listen to instruction and be guided by wisdom?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, put the fear of You within me, so that I will not live by myself but honor You as Lord in every place. Help me receive wisdom, accept instruction, and discern well, so that my choices each day will walk in the path that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Forsaking the Spring of Living Water Leaves Life Dry and Cracked
v: The LORD says, “What unrighteousness have your fathers found in me, that they have gone far from me, and have walked after worthless vanity, and have become worthless?

They didn’t say, ‘Where is the LORD who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and of pits, through a land of drought and of the shadow of death, through a land that no one passed through, and where no man lived?’
I brought you into a plentiful land to eat its fruit and its goodness; but when you entered, you defiled my land, and made my heritage an abomination.

The priests didn’t say, ‘Where is the LORD?’ and those who handle the law didn’t know me. The rulers also transgressed against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal and followed things that do not profit.
“Therefore I will yet contend with you,” says the LORD, “and I will contend with your children’s children.
For pass over to the islands of Kittim, and see. Send to Kedar, and consider diligently, and see if there has been such a thing.
Has a nation changed its gods, which really are no gods? But my people have changed their glory for that which doesn’t profit.
“Be astonished, you heavens, at this and be horribly afraid. Be very desolate,” says the LORD.
“For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut out cisterns for themselves: broken cisterns that can’t hold water.
b: :5 The Lord says this: What unrighteousness did your fathers find in me, that they went far from me, followed worthless gods, and themselves became worthless? 2:6 They did not say, “Where is the Lord who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and pits, a land of drought and deep darkness, a land no one passed through and where no one lived?” 2:7 I brought you into a plentiful land, to eat its fruit and its goodness; but when you entered, you defiled my land and made my inheritance an abomination. 2:8 The priests did not say, “Where is the Lord?” Those who handled the law did not know me. The rulers transgressed against me; the prophets prophesied by Baal and followed things that do not profit. 2:9 The Lord says: Therefore I will contend with you, and I will contend with your children’s children. 2:10 Cross over to the islands of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and consider carefully; see whether such a thing has ever happened. 2:11 Has a nation ever changed its gods, which really are no gods? But my people have exchanged their glory for that which does not profit. 2:12 Be astonished at this, you heavens, be horribly afraid, be utterly desolate! says the Lord. 2:13 For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living water, and have dug cisterns for themselves, broken cisterns that can hold no water.

This passage is God’s deep accusation and sorrow over his people. He is not speaking to the nations but to his own people, asking, “Why have you forsaken me?” God had brought them out of slavery, through the barren, dry wilderness, and into a land rich with promise. Yet once they entered abundance, they forgot the God who rescued them, pursued emptiness and idols, and even exchanged God’s glory for things of no benefit.

What is most heartbreaking is not the ignorance of the people but the silence and decline of the spiritual leaders. The priests no longer asked, “Where is the Lord?” Those who handled the law did not know him, and the prophets turned to the false Baal. God calls this a great evil, because they “forsook the spring of living water” and “dug broken cisterns for themselves,” thinking they could store water, not knowing they would run dry.

A life that belongs to God does not depend on man-made security or religious form, but on staying vitally connected to God. He is the spring of living water, who ceaselessly supplies, cleanses, refreshes, and renews our lives. When people no longer revere him or seek him, they lose not only God’s blessing but also slide into spiritual dryness and collapse.
a: Examine whether you still long for God or have turned to emptiness
Is your heart still looking for God’s presence? Or has it been taken over by busyness, habit, and self?
Don’t let your spiritual life shrink to mere form; return to a real relationship with God
Don’t be content with past grace; keep coming back to God to drink living water.
Connect with God actively every day, and don’t live on your own “broken cisterns”
What do you lean on to face pressure? God’s living water, or man-made security?
q: Am I still beside the spring of living water today, or have I wandered off to look for things that do not profit? Is my spiritual life vibrant or dry?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, forgive me for so often leaving You to look for other satisfaction, not realizing they are empty, cracked cisterns. Draw me back to You, the spring of living water, so that I long for You and draw near to You, and no longer go dry but am refreshed and renewed daily by Your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Lord Knows Your Weakness, Yet Intercedes for You and Strengthens You
v: “But you are those who have continued with me in my trials.
I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,
that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”
The Lord said, “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have all of you, that he might sift you as wheat,
but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.”
He said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”
He said, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times.”
b: These are the words Jesus spoke to his disciples at the Last Supper, just before his arrest, in a tone full of tenderness and deep preparation. Jesus first affirms that the disciples have stayed with him through his trials, a sign of faithfulness, and promises that they will share his glory in the kingdom. Then he turns to Peter and says, in the most personal way, “Simon, Simon!” This is not just a form of address; it is a call of warning, spoken in love.

Jesus knew Peter would fail, and knew Satan was preparing to test him, yet he did not give up on Peter. Instead he said, “I prayed for you.” This is the heart of Jesus as our High Priest: he knows human weakness, yet still intercedes and guards our faith so that it is not completely lost. Even though Peter would fall, Jesus had already prepared his restoration and entrusted him to strengthen others in the future.

This is the reality of a life that belongs to God: we do not stand firm on our own, but by Jesus’ intercession, the Holy Spirit’s support, and God’s faithfulness. God does not demand that you never fail; he calls you, even after you fall, to turn back, be restored, answer the call again, and go on to uphold more people.
a: Accept your weakness and hand it over to the Lord
Don’t pretend to be strong, and don’t blame yourself for being weak; the Lord knows all about you and has already prayed for you.
After failing, return to the Lord and let him restore your faith and calling
Falling is not the fearful thing; refusing to turn back is. The Lord is still waiting for you and has prepared a path of new life.
Become a source of strength in others’ lives
After you experience God’s forgiveness and restoration, don’t stay in self-blame; become a companion who supports others in their difficulties.
q: Do I often lose faith because of my weakness? Am I willing to believe the Lord is still interceding for me and that I can still be useful in his hands?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for knowing my weakness and still interceding for me and holding me so that my faith does not fail. Help me turn back after I fall and experience Your restoration, and help me uphold others, so that we all stand firm in Your grace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Offer Yourself as a Living Sacrifice and Live a Life That Pleases God
v: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.
Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

For I say through the grace that was given me, to everyone who is among you, not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think; but to think reasonably, as God has apportioned to each person a measure of faith.
b: Here Paul calls believers to respond to God in a way that is both challenging and loving. He does not command; he builds on “the mercies of God,” reminding us that since we have been saved by the grace of Jesus, our lives should be an act of worship: not merely praise from our lips, but presenting our “bodies,” that is, our whole selves, our whole lives, our entire being, completely to God.

This offering is not a one-time event but a “living sacrifice”: every day we live for the glory of God and let him be King in us. A life that belongs to God begins with selflessness: not living for ourselves, but letting God’s will guide us each day. When we live this way, we enter true worship, which is not only “reasonable” but the very purpose for which we were made.

Next, Paul reminds us not to be shaped by the values of this world, but to let our minds be renewed and enter God’s point of view. Not looking to circumstances or to what others do, but daily, through God’s word and the light of the Holy Spirit, testing and practicing that “good, well-pleasing, and perfect” will.

Finally, he points out specifically: do not exalt yourself, and do not put yourself down; see yourself rightly according to the measure of faith God has given. Such a life is humble, renewed, and belongs to God.
a: Put yourself in God’s hands and become a vessel he can use every day
Not only in Sunday worship, but letting every day, every matter, and every choice become an offering of worship.
Let God’s word renew you, and stop conforming to the world
Don’t live by the world’s trends and standards; measure values and choices with God’s eyes.
Learn humility, and accept the faith and role God has given you
Don’t compare yourself with others or see yourself as too high or too low; place yourself by God’s grace and fulfill your mission.
q: Have I truly given myself completely to God? In daily life, am I guided by God’s will rather than the voices of the world?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I want to offer myself to You as a living sacrifice, not only in words of worship but in obedience in my life. Renew my mind so that I am not pulled along by the world, but clearly understand and live out Your will. Help me humbly fulfill the role You have entrusted to me, to the glory of Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Open Your Hand and Live Out God’s Kindness and Mercy
v: At the end of every seven years, you shall cancel debts.

This is the way it shall be done: every creditor shall release that which he has lent to his neighbor. He shall not require payment from his neighbor and his brother, because the LORD’s release has been proclaimed.
Of a foreigner you may require it; but whatever of yours is with your brother, your hand shall release.
However there will be no poor with you (for the LORD will surely bless you in the land which the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance to possess)
if only you diligently listen to the LORD your God’s voice, to observe to do all this commandment which I command you today.
For the LORD your God will bless you, as he promised you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
If a poor man, one of your brothers, is with you within any of your gates in your land which the LORD your God gives you, you shall not harden your heart, nor shut your hand from your poor brother;
but you shall surely open your hand to him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need, which he lacks.

Beware that there not be a wicked thought in your heart, saying, “The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand,” and your eye be evil against your poor brother and you give him nothing; and he cry to the LORD against you, and it be sin to you.
You shall surely give, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give to him, because it is for this thing the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in all that you put your hand to.
For the poor will never cease out of the land. Therefore I command you to surely open your hand to your brother, to your needy, and to your poor, in your land.
b: In this passage God established for Israel an institution of great kindness and wisdom: every seventh year there was to be a release, in which people let go of one another and no longer pursued debts. This was not only an economic reset but a training in the culture of God’s Kingdom: learning to treat others with God’s mercy and grace.

In today’s world, full of self-interest and calculation, God’s word reminds us to “open your hand” rather than close it and look away. He says, “If your brother is in need, do not be cold toward him; supply what he lacks.” This is not out of duty but out of reverence for God and imitation of his character. God himself is the One who forgave our debts, and having been forgiven, we should be glad to give.

God does not only command us to give; he wants us to give without a grieved heart. What he values is not the amount but our attitude. If we give willingly, he promises to bless everything we put our hands to, making us an outlet of blessing and not a dead end.

This is a life that belongs to God: not centered on ourselves, but letting God’s mercy live in our hands, our time, and our money. When we give willingly and generously, we truly live out “letting Jesus be King,” living his character out among people.
a: Learn to give generously, not only money but also care and companionship
Who is the “needy brother” around you? God calls you to “open your hand” to them.
Give without hesitation or calculation, only to please God
Do not let selfishness or holding back block God’s blessing; when you give, God fills you even more.
See money and resources as entrusted by God, not to hoard for yourself but to bless others
Everything you have is God’s grace; are you willing to be a channel for him?
q: Am I glad to help those in need? In giving, is my heart free and joyful? Is God’s mercy flowing through me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for never being stingy and for always supplying all I need. Give me a generous heart, so that I am willing to see those in need through Your eyes and help them with joy. May I live in Your grace and also live out Your kindness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: God Himself Equips You to Complete the Work He Has Entrusted to You
v: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Behold, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all kinds of workmanship,
to devise skillful works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in bronze,
and in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving of wood, to work in all kinds of workmanship.

Behold, I myself have appointed with him Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the heart of all who are wise-hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded you:
b: In the sacred task of building the tabernacle, God did not give Moses only the blueprint; he personally chose and equipped the people to carry it out. He named Bezalel and Oholiab and explained that he had “filled them with his Spirit,” giving heavenly wisdom and skill so they could do the work he entrusted to them.

This shows us that God’s work never begins with people’s natural ability but with God’s calling and equipping. Whether it was metalwork, woodcarving, or setting gems, these seemingly technical tasks were spiritual service in God’s eyes. True service does not divide things into “sacred” and “secular”; the question is whether you are willing to be used by God and to carry it out according to his heart.

This is a life that belongs to God: placing all our talents, gifts, and resources in the Lord’s hands and letting him use them. Whether you are preaching, leading worship, or working in an office, on a building site, or in a kitchen, if you act according to God’s heart, it is worship and it is holy work. Letting Jesus be King is not only on the platform, but in every task your hands faithfully complete.
a: Believe that God has prepared a role and a task for you
You did not appear in this generation by chance, and your gifts are not random; God has tailor-made his assignment for you.
Be willing for God’s Spirit to fill you and take you beyond your natural limits
Relying on yourself, you are limited; relying on God, there is no limit. Ask that God’s Spirit not only move you but also equip you personally.
See every job as an opportunity to serve
Do not look down on your workplace, daily routine, craft, or small details; when you offer them up for God’s use, they carry eternal value.
q: Am I willing to place my abilities and resources in God’s hands? Do I believe God wants to use me to fulfill his plan?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for not only calling me but personally equipping me. Fill me with Your Spirit so that I have wisdom and ability from You to complete the work You have entrusted to me. May all that my hands do, big or small, please You and be a witness to Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Live in the World but Not Of It, Set Apart for the Truth
v: Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you;
even as you gave him authority over all flesh, so he will give eternal life to all whom you have given him.
This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.
Now, Father, glorify me with your own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed.
But now I come to you, and I say these things in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves.
I have given them your word. The world hated them because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
I pray not that you would take them from the world, but that you would keep them from the evil one.
They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, even so I have sent them into the world.
For their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.
b: This is the prayer Jesus prayed before going to the cross, the heartfelt intercession to the Father for his disciples and for everyone who would later believe in him. He did not ask the Father to take us out of the world, but to keep us from the snare of the evil one while we are in it, so that we may be set apart by the truth.

This is a profound calling: to live in the world but not be of the world. Jesus says we are sent, we have a mission, just as he was sent by the Father. This is not escaping the world, but living a set-apart life in the world, living out the truth and the glory of the Father.

A life that belongs to God is not withdrawal or compromise, but placing ourselves fully in God’s hands and letting God’s word be the standard of our lives, the foundation of our values, and the measure of our decisions. We are chosen by God, entrusted by Jesus, and set apart by the truth. When we let God’s word adjust our hearts, we can stand firm in a world full of temptation and pressure and live out our identity and mission as God’s people.
a: If you are not of the world, don’t let the world’s values become your standard
Stay alert in daily life: are my choices based on God’s word or on worldly habits?
Take the initiative to let God’s word cleanse, renew, and adjust your life
Reading, meditating on, and practicing Scripture daily is not just knowledge, but being sanctified by the truth.
Understand that you exist for a mission, not merely for comfort
Your presence in your family, workplace, and community has God’s sending and purpose.
q: Am I truly willing to be set apart by God’s truth? Am I living a life that is “not of the world” yet “sent for the world”?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing Your heart for us through Jesus’ prayer. Keep me from being defiled in this world, and let Your word be a lamp to my feet and a light on my path. Help me be set apart by the truth and live as a witness to Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Give All Victory to the God Who Strengthens My Hands
v: The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,
even the God who executes vengeance for me, who brings down peoples under me,
who brings me away from my enemies. Yes, you lift me up above those who rise up against me. You deliver me from the violent man.
Therefore I will give thanks to you, LORD, among the nations, and will sing praises to your name.
He gives great deliverance to his king, and shows loving kindness to his anointed, to David and to his offspring, forever more.”
b: This is the song of thanksgiving David sang to God in his later years. Looking back over a lifetime of battles, flights, and ups and downs, he no longer boasts of his own ability or experience but gives all the glory to God. David calls God the “living God” and “the rock of my salvation,” because he knows that without God’s rescue and support over his enemies, he could not have survived to this day on his own.

This attitude of faith is also a mark of a life that belongs to God: not boasting of how strong we are, but humbly acknowledging that all victory, protection, and glory are God’s doing. David’s life was not always smooth, but he chose to sum up his journey with worship and thanksgiving, which is the mark of walking with God.

God is not only the rock and savior in our personal lives; he is the Lord who vindicates us and works all things together for good. His faithfulness and love do not stop with our generation but continue to our descendants, just as he promised David, a love that lasts forever.
a: When looking back on life, focus on what God has done, not on your own effort
We easily forget that it is God who kept us in secret, held us up on the heights, and carried us in the valleys.
Turn every victory and breakthrough into worship and thanksgiving
Don’t keep the glory for yourself; like David, lift up God’s name before all.
Place your hope in God’s unchanging love
God’s plan for your life will not end; what he has promised he will fulfill, for generation after generation.
q: Am I in the habit of giving credit to God? When facing opposition and challenges, can I still praise him and trust what he is doing?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being my rock and my savior in my life. It is not that I stand on my own, but that You hold me up, protect me, and reach out to rescue me. May my life be a testimony of Your grace, and I want to give all glory and victory to You, forever and ever. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When the King Rules in Righteousness, the People Have Security and a Clear Heart
v: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.
A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.
The eyes of those who see will not be dim, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
The heart of the rash will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers will be ready to speak plainly.
b: This passage is a prophecy and hope concerning the Messiah’s kingdom: there will be a King who rules in righteousness, and what he brings is not oppression and chaos but justice and peace. The governing he carries out will turn around and heal all of society and the human heart.

This King points to our Lord Jesus Christ. He is not only King in heaven; he longs to be King in each of our lives. When he reigns within us, our hearts are secure; when we let his standard guide our living, we find shelter in the storm, refreshing in the drought, and shade in weariness.

This is a life that belongs to God: not controlling life by ourselves, but letting Jesus reign in our hearts, letting his word be what we lean on, and letting the Holy Spirit guide our direction. In this way we can move from confusion to clarity, from closed to open, from rashness to wisdom.
a: Settle it again every day
Letting Jesus reign in my life means I don’t decide the direction; I humbly seek the Lord’s leading and rule.
When circumstances are hard, don’t lean on yourself; take refuge in this righteous King
He is the shelter of my heart, and his word is the spring and comfort in my trouble.
Receive renewal and clarity from the Lord
Let God’s truth heal our eyes, ears, and hearts, so that we can see clearly, hear, understand, and speak out God’s will.
q: Today, am I willing to truly hand over authority to this righteous King? Is there still confusion and wandering in my heart that needs his rule and renewal?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I want the King You have appointed, the Lord Jesus Christ, to reign in my heart. Give me peace under Your rule and clarity in Your word. May I not rely on my own judgment but walk each step by Your guidance. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Keep Praying in an Unjust World, and God Will Vindicate You
v: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray and not give up,
saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God and didn’t respect man.
A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’
He wouldn’t for a while; but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect man,
yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
The Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
Won’t God avenge his chosen ones who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?
I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
b: In this passage Jesus uses the story of the widow and the unjust judge to teach the disciples to pray always and not lose heart. A widow was among the most vulnerable in that society, with no one to speak for her, yet through her persistent pleading she wore down even a judge who neither feared God nor respected people, and in the end he defended her.

Jesus stresses that the heavenly Father is completely different from the unjust judge. God is loving and righteous; he hears the cry of his chosen ones and promises to vindicate them quickly. This reminds us that when we face injustice and hardship in the world, we must not give up calling on God, because God sees, God knows, and God will bring rescue in his time.

But the Lord also raises a challenge: “When the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?” He is looking not for those who pray with a moment of passion, but for disciples who are willing to keep trusting through a long wait. Such people are those who truly let God be King and let God carry out his justice.
a: When you see no change, choose to keep praying
God’s silence is not indifference; he is accomplishing a better plan.
Entrust your grievances to God and don’t take revenge into your own hands
Trusting God is more powerful than winning a moment’s argument, for he is the Lord who vindicates us.
Make prayer a daily rhythm, not a last resort
Don’t wait for trouble to pray; talk with God every day and keep your faith firm.
q: Am I still holding on to prayer in faith? Or have I lost heart and drawn back because I have waited so long? Today, God invites me to come back to him once more.
pr: Dear heavenly Father, You are a righteous God who never ignores the cries of Your children. When I am discouraged and disappointed, strengthen my faith so that I do not stop praying or lose hope. Help me believe that the vindication You promised will surely come, and in the waiting help me live in reverence and obedience to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Lord Does Not Leave Us as Orphans; He Sends the Holy Spirit as the Indwelling Helper
v: If you love me, keep my commandments.
I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever:
the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive, for it doesn’t see him and doesn’t know him. You know him, for he lives with you and will be in you.
I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.
Yet a little while, and the world will see me no more; but you will see me. Because I live, you will live also.
In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
One who has my commandments and keeps them, that person is one who loves me. One who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will reveal myself to him.”
Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, “Lord, what has happened that you are about to reveal yourself to us, and not to the world?”
Jesus answered him, “If a man loves me, he will keep my word. My Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him.
He who doesn’t love me doesn’t keep my words. The word which you hear isn’t mine, but the Father’s who sent me.
“I have said these things to you while still living with you.
But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.
b: One of Jesus’ deepest concerns before leaving this world was to assure his disciples that he would not abandon them or leave them like helpless orphans. He promised to send the “Counselor,” the Holy Spirit, to be with us forever, not only as an outside helper but as an indwelling teacher and comforter.

He calls the Spirit “the Spirit of truth,” meaning the Spirit comes not only to bring power but to guide us into God’s truth so that we can understand, remember, and practice Jesus’ words. This is why Jesus says, “He who has my commandments, and keeps them, that person is he who loves me.” True love is not only an expression of feeling but obedience and action in daily life.

Jesus says that those who love him and keep his word will not only be loved by the Father but will experience the dwelling of the triune God: the Father and the Son will make their home in the believer, and the Holy Spirit is the guarantee and channel of that presence. What a great grace: we do not struggle alone in the world, but have the Holy Spirit living in us and walking with us every day, helping us live a life that belongs to God.
a: Seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance in everything
Facing choices, difficulties, or doubts, don’t act from the flesh; first be still, pray, and wait, and let the Holy Spirit speak.
Let your love for the Lord show up in obedience
Don’t stop at saying you love the Lord; keep his word in your actions and live in a way that fits his heart.
Build a daily habit of fellowship with the Holy Spirit
The Holy Spirit is not just a prompting that appears in meetings, but God himself, whom you can draw near to, learn from, and be reminded by every day.
q: Am I living like an “orphan,” or like a child of God who knows the Lord is with me? Am I willing to let the Holy Spirit teach and renew me every day?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for not leaving me an orphan but sending the Holy Spirit to be with me forever. Teach me not to rely on myself but to live by the Spirit who dwells in me. Let my love for You not stay in my words but be willing to keep Your word, walking with You in every day of my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Raised Up for Such a Time as This: Stand Courageously in the Gap
v: Then Esther spoke to Hathach, and gave him a message to Mordecai:

“All the king’s servants and the people of the king’s provinces know that whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”
They told Esther’s words to Mordecai.
Then Mordecai asked them to return this answer to Esther: “Don’t think to yourself that you will escape in the king’s house any more than all the Jews.

For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
Then Esther asked them to answer Mordecai,

“Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Susa, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day. I and my maidens will also fast the same way. Then I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.”
b: This passage is the pivotal moment of the book of Esther. Facing the crisis of the Jewish people’s coming destruction, Mordecai points out a truth: God’s deliverance will surely come, but are you willing to be the vessel God uses? Your position, your background, and the place you hold now may be exactly what God has prepared for this moment.

At first Esther also had her fear and struggle. Being queen brought honor, but entering the king’s court did not mean absolute safety. She faced a life-or-death choice: protect herself and stay silent, or risk speaking up and stand in the gap for God’s people?

What is moving is that Esther finally answered, “If I perish, I perish.” This is the courage of self-denial, strength that comes from obeying God. She understood that what she had was not for her own safety but for fulfilling God’s greater purpose.

This is also the lesson for everyone who belongs to God: the position we hold today, whether in the workplace, family, or community, may be the strategic place God has set for this moment. He calls us not merely to live comfortably but to respond courageously to his heart and become a vessel standing in the gap.
a: Recognize that your present position is God’s arrangement
Don’t look down on where you are; it may be exactly where God wants to use you.
Facing crisis, don’t run away; enter prayer and fasting
Like Esther, when we humble ourselves before God, we gain strength to take the key action.
Respond courageously to God’s call, even if the cost is your former comfort
When you stand up, God will use you to accomplish more than you ask or imagine.
q: Am I willing to be someone God can use to stand in the gap in this generation? Am I willing to lay down my own security and plans for God’s purpose?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I know You call me not to live only for myself but to be a vessel in Your hands. Give me courage and faith not to shrink back in a crisis, but to stand up boldly at the critical moment and pray and act for the people, the matters, and the Kingdom You love. May my life be used by You, just as Esther was raised up for such a time. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Discipleship at the End of the Age: Watchful in Prayer, Loving One Another, Faithful in Service
v: But the end of all things is near. Therefore be of sound mind, self-controlled, and sober in prayer.
And above all things be earnest in your love among yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.

If anyone speaks, let it be as it were the very words of God. If anyone serves, let it be as of the strength which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
b: When Peter wrote these words, he knew well that Christians were living in a turbulent world. He reminds believers: “The end of all things is near.” This is not meant to frighten but to remind us to seize the present and turn our eyes from the temporary to the eternal. Because the day of the Lord’s return is near, our life on earth should be more watchful, more purposeful, and more loving.

First, he encourages believers to be self-controlled and watchful in prayer. This means guarding our thoughts and keeping connected with God, making prayer our daily breathing. Not seeking God only in emergencies, but cultivating heavenly sensitivity in ordinary days.

Second, Peter stresses: “Above all things be earnest in your love among yourselves,” for love covers a multitude of sins. This is not covering up wrongs, but bearing with and supporting one another in love, not quickly condemning or keeping score of faults. When we treat each other with love, we experience repair in brokenness and unity in weakness.

Finally, he calls believers to use their gifts to serve one another as good stewards of God’s grace. Whether preaching, hospitality, labor, or caring, all are trusts received from God. We do not work by our own strength but rely on the strength God supplies, so that in all things God may be glorified.
This is a life that belongs to God: in the last days, not afraid, not cold, not drawing back, but watchful, loving, and serving, living out each day as a witness of living for the Lord.
a: Make prayer the foundation of your life
Set aside time each day to talk with God, and don’t let busyness steal your desire to be close to the Lord.
Love one another in practical action
Start with accepting, bearing with, forgiving, and serving, and let love be the bond of the church and the family.
Use your gifts to bless people
Don’t bury your talents; the gifts God gave you were prepared to serve others and glorify God.
q: Am I living like someone who knows the Lord is coming soon? Am I watchful in prayer, earnest in love, and faithful in service?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for letting me know the end of all things is near, not to make me afraid, but to remind me to be watchful, to love people, and to serve. Add to my strength so that I live not by myself but by the grace and power You give, and faithfully complete the mission You have entrusted to me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Relying on the Name of the Lord Is True Security
v: The LORD’s name is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.
The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, like an unscalable wall in his own imagination.
b: These two proverbs draw a sharp contrast between two sources of “security.” One is the righteous person, who makes God’s name his refuge; the other is the rich person, who makes wealth his safety net.

“The name of the Lord is a strong tower” means that God’s presence and authority are our true protection in danger. Just as strong walls protected people in ancient times, God’s name is an indestructible refuge. When the righteous face a storm, they do not rely on running away or on their own strength, but “run to” God’s name: entering into relationship with God and hiding under his faithfulness and love.

By contrast, the rich man “imagines” that his wealth is like a high wall protecting him, but that is a false sense of security. Possessions matter, but they cannot truly secure life, heal the heart, or face death and eternity. When trouble comes, no amount of resources can replace God’s keeping.

This passage reminds us that a life that belongs to God is not built on the world’s guarantees but finds true security in God’s presence. The name of the Lord is his character, his works, and his salvation; whoever trusts in him will never be put to shame.
a: In anxiety, run first to God rather than looking for outside support
God’s name gives us a peace beyond people and things; it is the true firm foundation of the heart.
Learn to recognize what you depend on
Ask yourself: when I am afraid, do I first think of God, or of money, status, and experience?
Practice trust daily
Don’t run to God only in a crisis; keep learning to trust and depend on him in everyday life.
q: What does my heart truly depend on? Do I make God the first refuge I run to?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, Your name is a strong tower, my true refuge in hard times. Help me not to rely on passing things, but in every anxiety and unease to learn to run to You and trust You. May my heart know deeply: having You with me is my greatest security. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Even When Regarded as the Scum of the World, Stay Faithful to the Lord to the End
v: For I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last of all, like men sentenced to death. For we are made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and men.
We are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You have honor, but we have dishonor.
Even to this present hour we hunger, thirst, are naked, are beaten, and have no certain dwelling place.
We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure.
Being defamed, we entreat. We are made as the filth of the world, the dirt wiped off by all, even until now.
b: In these words, the apostle Paul uses striking language to describe the suffering and shame he and the other apostles endured for the Lord. They were not respected leaders but like prisoners at the end of the parade, dragged onto the stage as a spectacle for all. They seemed foolish, weak, and pitiful, and were even treated by the world as worthless scum.

This is not self-pity or accusation, but a shift in values seen from God’s perspective. A life in Christ does not seek glory and position but walks a path of self-denial, service, and bearing disgrace. Paul says, “We toil, working with our own hands. When people curse us, we bless. Being persecuted, we endure. Being defamed, we entreat.” Such a response is not human instinct but love and steadfastness that come from God.

This reminds us that a life that belongs to God is not about earthly glory but about faithfully completing what God has entrusted. Even if we are looked down on, misunderstood, or excluded, as long as it is for the Lord’s sake, it has eternal value. This is the life of letting Jesus be King: not living for ourselves, but living for the glory of God.
a: Don’t measure success and honor by the world’s standards
Faithfulness matters more than achievement; suffering for the Lord is extremely precious in God’s eyes.
When facing persecution and misunderstanding, choose to respond with love
Learn from Paul not to repay evil for evil, but to hold on to gentleness and patience.
Even in the lowliest position, serve faithfully
What God values is your faithfulness in hardship, not outward glitter and applause.
q: Am I willing to be misunderstood or even looked down on for the Lord’s sake? Am I still faithfully living out the identity and mission God has entrusted to me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for choosing me to be part of Your Kingdom. Keep me from seeking human glory and make me long for Your delight. Even when I am not valued in the eyes of the world, may I still stand for You, endure for You, and bear witness for You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: In the Deepest Sorrow, We Can Still Wait for God’s Mercy and Vindication
v: For the Lord will not cast off forever.
For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.
To crush under foot all the prisoners of the earth,
to turn away the right of a man before the face of the Most High,
to subvert a man in his cause, the Lord doesn’t approve.
Who is he who says, and it comes to pass, when the Lord doesn’t command it?
Doesn’t evil and good come out of the mouth of the Most High?
Why should a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?
Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the LORD.
Let’s lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens.
“We have transgressed and have rebelled. You have not pardoned.
Lord, you have pleaded the causes of my soul. You have redeemed my life.
LORD, you have seen my wrong. Judge my cause.
b: This passage comes out of Jeremiah’s great grief over the fall of Jerusalem and the exile of the people. Yet in the midst of sorrow and ruin, he utters a word of deep faith: “The Lord will not cast off forever.”

God’s heart does not delight in punishing and tearing down, but in showing mercy when people repent. Though he causes grief, he also “has compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses,” because he does not afflict willingly. This is not merely emotional comfort, but a firm knowledge of God’s righteous and loving nature.

The passage also points out that when disaster comes, we should not blame God or complain about others, but “search and examine our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” When we sincerely lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we will experience his gracious hand supporting us again.

By verse 58, Jeremiah declares: “Lord, you have pleaded the causes of my soul. You have redeemed my life.” This is the turning point of faith, from confessing sin to relying on God’s rescue and vindication. It is not only a personal experience of salvation but also the hope of a nation turning back.
a: Do not lose faith in God in hardship
Even when he seems silent, God’s mercy runs deep; he does not afflict you willingly.
Be willing to reflect on yourself in brokenness and turn to God
Hardship is an opportunity for self-examination, not to push us away from God but to bring us closer to him.
Believe that God is the One who vindicates and rescues you
Don’t argue or take revenge on your own; entrust your wrongs to him, and he will set them right in justice.
q: When I go through pain and injustice, can I still believe in God’s love and rescue? Am I willing to examine myself first, and then trust his vindication?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that though You cause grief, You do not cast me off. Help me, in hardship, to turn my eyes to You, reflect on my conduct, repent sincerely, and entrust all my wrongs into Your hands. You are the Lord who rescues me and the God who vindicates me, and I will trust in You all my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Cast Your Burden on God, and He Will Sustain You to the End
v: Attend to me, and answer me. I am restless in my complaint, and moan
because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked. For they bring suffering on me. In anger they hold a grudge against me.
My heart is severely pained within me. The terrors of death have fallen on me.
Fearfulness and trembling have come on me. Horror has overwhelmed me.
As for me, I will call on God. The LORD will save me.
Evening, morning, and at noon, I will cry out in distress. He will hear my voice.
He has redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, although there are many who oppose me.
God, who is enthroned forever, will hear and answer them. Selah. They never change and don’t fear God.
He raises his hands against his friends. He has violated his covenant.
His mouth was smooth as butter, but his heart was war. His words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords.
Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
But you, God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. Bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their days, but I will trust in you.
b: This is a psalm David wrote in pain and betrayal. His enemies were not only outside attackers but also the fear within and a wounded heart. He says, “My heart is severely pained within me. The terrors of death have fallen on me,” and even wants to escape reality, flying away like a dove.

Yet David did not choose to run away; he chose to pray. He says, “I will call on God. The Lord will save me.” This was not a moment’s impulse but a continual crying out, morning, noon, and evening. Prayer is not only the release of words but an expression of faith: believing that God still hears and is still in control.

The most moving line in this psalm is: “Cast your burden on the Lord and he will sustain you.” We often think we must carry all of life’s pressures ourselves, but God invites us to learn to entrust, to hand over the burden that weighs us down. He will not let the righteous be moved; he will personally sustain us to the end.
a: In hardship, actively seek God rather than escape
Bring your emotions to God, not suppressing them or venting them, but sincerely entrusting them and trusting him.
Build a habit of continual prayer
Don’t pray only in emergencies; walk with God day and night, making prayer as natural as breathing.
Learn to entrust, and stop carrying the burden yourself
When you cast your burden on God, you will find that his hand is more able to bear it than your shoulders.
q: Have I given my worries and burdens to God, or am I still holding everything up myself? Today, am I willing to choose prayer and choose dependence on him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when my heart is in pain and fear surrounds me, I want to cry out to You as David did. Hear my prayer, take the burden of my life, and keep me from being shaken. You are the God who sustains me, and I want to depend on You all my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Living in the Lord’s Love and Bearing the Fruit of Loving One Another
v: Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love.
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, even as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.
I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full.
“This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you.
Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends if you do whatever I command you.
No longer do I call you servants, for the servant doesn’t know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father, I have made known to you.

You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.
“I command these things to you, that you may love one another.
b: This passage is Jesus’ parting charge to his disciples, full of deep affection and trust. He begins, “Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you.” What a stunning declaration! We are loved with the very same love the Father has for the Son. This love is complete, eternal, and unshakable.

But the Lord’s love is not meant to leave us simply basking in the feeling of being loved. He calls us to “remain in his love,” to live in the relationship of this love. How do we remain? Jesus gives a clear answer: “If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love.” He is not asking for legalism, but for a willing obedience to his word that flows from loving and trusting him.

And the heart of this commandment is to love one another. “Even as I have loved you”—the Lord’s love is a sacrificial love that lays down its life for friends. He calls us his friends, and he has chosen us to go and bear fruit. A true disciple does not only receive grace, but also bears the fruit of love, letting the Lord’s love flow out through us.
a: Practice living in the Lord’s love every day
It is not enough to know that God loves me; I respond to his love in practice, depend on him, and walk with him.
Let obedience be the concrete expression of loving the Lord
Not only affection in the heart, but action that carries out the Lord’s words.
Live out mutual love as a witness in your relationships
Love does not wait for others to change first. It gives first, bears with others first, and lays down self first.
q: Do I often remain in the Lord’s love? Do I live out his love, even toward those who are hard to love?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that through the love of Jesus Christ You called me, chose me, and named me Your friend. I want to remain in Your love, to learn obedience and to love others. Cause me to bear fruit that lasts, so that Your love may flow through me into the lives of others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Values of the Kingdom: A Path of Blessing That Begins in the Heart
v: Seeing the multitudes, he went up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him.
He opened his mouth and taught them, saying,
“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
b: This passage is known as the Beatitudes. It opens the Sermon on the Mount and paints a picture of the character of the people of the Kingdom. It is far from the values of the world. The ones the Lord calls “blessed” are not those who look successful or self-made, but those who are willing to let God be King and who turn to God from the heart in repentance.

“Blessed are the poor in spirit” means knowing that we are spiritually empty and need God’s grace. “Blessed are those who mourn” speaks of grieving over sin and being heartbroken over the brokenness of the world. The gentle, those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, the pure in heart… these are not natural temperaments, but a God-given life that grows out of connection with God.

The Beatitudes are not conditions for entering heaven; they are the fruit of a life that belongs to God. When we center on the Lord and take his standard as our standard, we begin to live a distinctive life. This is the beginning of God’s divine order: not character polished by our own effort, but a change from the inside out that starts with obeying the Holy Spirit.
a: Examine whether your values match the standard of the Kingdom
We often measure people by achievement, but God values a poor spirit, a hunger for righteousness, and deeds of mercy.
Hold on to righteousness and peace under pressure and persecution
When you are persecuted for righteousness, it is not failure. It is sharing in the Lord’s glory.
Let the Holy Spirit work in your life to shape you as a citizen of the Kingdom
Not by dressing yourself up with good behavior, but by being willing to be changed, pruned, and renewed by God.
q: Am I living as a citizen of the Kingdom? What am I longing for? What am I depending on? When I face the world, am I willing to choose God’s way?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for the Beatitudes Jesus taught, which show me that the way of the Kingdom is not worldly glory but a path of blessing that turns the heart toward You. Make my spirit humble and ever hungry for Your righteousness. Help me to firmly choose Your standard over the values of the world and to live the life that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Commit Your Way to the Lord, and He Will Bring Justice for You
v: Commit your way to the LORD. Trust also in him, and he will do this:
he will make your righteousness shine out like light, and your justice as the noon day sun.
Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
Cease from anger, and forsake wrath. Don’t fret; it leads only to evildoing.
For evildoers shall be cut off, but those who wait for the LORD shall inherit the land.
For yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more. Yes, though you look for his place, he isn’t there.
But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
The wicked plots against the just, and gnashes at him with his teeth.
The Lord will laugh at him, for he sees that his day is coming.
The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, to kill those who are upright on the path.
Their sword shall enter into their own heart. Their bows shall be broken.
Better is a little that the righteous has, than the abundance of many wicked.
For the arms of the wicked shall be broken, but the LORD upholds the righteous.
b: Psalm 37 is a song for people who struggle in an unjust age. It does not teach us to escape reality, but guides us in how to keep living a God-centered life amid chaos and a world where the wicked seem to have the upper hand.

The psalmist first reminds us: “Commit your way to Yahweh. Trust also in him, and he will do it.” In real life we may meet unfairness and injustice, and even see the wicked seem to prosper. But God asks us not to walk by sight. He asks us to rest in him and wait patiently for his work.

Again and again this passage stresses two qualities that belong to God: humility and patience. The way forward is not anger or revenge, but choosing to cease from anger and forsake wrath, because these emotions, if not committed to God, will only bring more harm. True security and abundance are what God gives to those who wait for him and trust in him.

As for the wicked who slander the righteous and draw their bows to set traps, they will in the end reap what they have sown. God does not forget the people he loves. He will step in, and he will stretch out his hand. The arms of the wicked will be broken, and though the righteous may have little, God upholds them. This is the lasting security.
a: When you meet injustice, hand the burden to God instead of defending yourself
Let God fight for you. His justice will in time shine like the noonday sun.
Learn to wait quietly in times of trouble and grow spiritual patience
Waiting is not just letting time pass. It is waiting for God to act, with no anger in your heart.
Choose humility and trust instead of following the world’s path of rivalry
True victory is God’s presence and support, not outward success or possessions.
q: Do I often rush to defend myself under pressure? Am I willing to commit my way to God and wait for his timing and his work?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that when I feel treated unfairly and confused, You are still the refuge of my heart. Teach me to commit everything to You, to stop my anger and my scheming, and to choose to wait quietly for Your timing. Strengthen me, that I may be a person who trusts You and walks in righteousness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Let the Holy Spirit Reign, and You Will Live in the Freedom and Glory of God’s Children
v: But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if it is so that the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if any man doesn’t have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.
If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.
So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh.
For if you live after the flesh, you must die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;
and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.
b: This passage takes us to the heart of the truth about the dignity of God’s children and their new life. True faith is not an outward religious performance. It is a change of life from the inside out, a renewal and leading that come because the Holy Spirit lives in us.

When the Spirit of God dwells in us, we are no longer controlled by the flesh and no longer live for selfish desires. The Spirit not only joins us to Christ, but also gives us strength to put to death the corrupt deeds of the old self and to live in a way that pleases God.

The foundation of all this is that in God’s eyes we are no longer slaves but his children. We do not need to earn love by performance, and we are no longer bound by fear, because the Spirit testifies within us that we are God’s children, and we can call him “Abba! Father!” in close intimacy. This is a tremendous grace and a change of identity.

To be God’s child means not only receiving new life but also becoming a joint heir with Christ. We may still go through suffering on earth, but that is the mark of walking the road of glory with Christ. In the end we will be glorified with the Lord. This is the glorious destiny God has prepared for us.
a: Ask the Holy Spirit to lead you each day instead of following your moods and desires
Let the Holy Spirit reign in your heart and lead you on the right path.
Keep in mind that you are God’s child, not a slave
Stop living in fear and self-accusation. God has accepted you as his beloved child.
See hope in suffering and share in glory with Christ
Do not lose heart because of suffering. It is a sign that you walk with the Lord, and the crown of glory will surely come.
q: Today, will my choices follow the flesh or listen to the Holy Spirit? Am I living in the freedom and glory of God’s children?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that through Jesus Christ You made me Your child and sent the Holy Spirit to live in me. Help me no longer to follow the old self and the flesh, but to live by the Spirit a life that pleases You. May I cry “Abba! Father!” to You each day under Your leading, and live out the dignity and glory of Your child. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Rejoice Always in the Lord, Learn Contentment, and Be Strong in Him
v: Rejoice in the Lord always! Again I will say, “Rejoice!”
Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand.
In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report: if there is any virtue and if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.
Do the things which you learned, received, heard, and saw in me, and the God of peace will be with you.
But I rejoice in the Lord greatly that now at length you have revived your thought for me; in which you did indeed take thought, but you lacked opportunity.
Not that I speak because of lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.
b: In a world filled with busyness and pressure, the apostle Paul wrote these words of peace and joy from prison. He was not urging people to cheer up when life is easy. He was living out a godly perspective and strength in the midst of hardship.

“Rejoice in the Lord always” is not an emotional slogan, but a choice of faith. True joy does not come from things going well, but from connection with the Lord. When we rejoice in the Lord, our hearts are not easily pushed around by circumstances.

Paul also reminds us that when we are anxious, the answer is not to suppress ourselves but to bring “everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving” to God. When we do, the peace that surpasses all understanding will guard our hearts and minds in Christ.

Finally, he shares a key practice: “I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.” This contentment is not passive resignation, but an active trust that, whether we have much or little, whether life is smooth or hard, having the Lord with us is enough. It is a strong life built up in the Lord.
a: Build your joy on the Lord, not on changing circumstances
Practice looking to the Lord and relying on him each day, and keep a hopeful outlook even in difficulty.
Learn to replace worry with prayer
Hand every concern to God, with a thankful heart that trusts he reigns and cares for you.
Learn contentment in every situation
This does not mean giving up on striving, but seeing each season from God’s point of view and trusting that his provision and timing are best.
q: Is the foundation of my joy built on the Lord? When I face lack, change, or pressure, can I respond with thanksgiving and prayer?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being with me in every circumstance. Give me a heart that rejoices always, that lives by trusting You and not by sight. When I am anxious, remind me to turn to prayer; when I am in need, teach me to be content and thankful. May the peace You give guard my heart every day. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: All Flesh Is Like Grass and Withers, but the Word of Our God Stands Forever
v: The voice of one saying, “Cry out!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field.
The grass withers, the flower fades, because the LORD’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”

You who tell good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who tell good news to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with strength! Lift it up! Don’t be afraid! Say to the cities of Judah, “Behold, your God!”
Behold, the Lord GOD will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.
b: This message from Isaiah is a poem, a letter announcing comfort, and a cry to wake up. Amid the noise of the world and the restlessness of the human heart, it reminds us that people and all their glory are like the flowers of the field, brief and fading. Only the word of God never changes and stands firm.

We are used to depending on our own abilities, outward advantages, human voices, and the applause of society. But the prophet says all of these are like grass and will surely wither. Only when we build our lives on God’s word can we stand firm in the midst of upheaval. His word is not just information. It is power, the very foundation of building God’s divine order.

Isaiah also announces a beautiful picture: God is not only a mighty King, but also a loving shepherd. He gathers the lambs in his arm and gently leads the fragile. He is not harsh or hurried. He is a God who sustains us with his eternal word and shepherds us with love.
a: Stop relying on what is passing and build your life on God’s word
Read Scripture daily, not only for knowledge, but so that God’s word becomes the foundation of your life.
Learn to give glory to the God who never changes
Do not exalt human achievement or get lost in how you feel about yourself, but honor God’s faithfulness and sovereignty.
Remember in hard times that God is your shepherd
