He is not a distant ruler. He is the loving Father who carries you and guides you every day.
q: Do I often build my life on grass and flowers that fade? Am I willing to set my heart again on God’s eternal word?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, Your word stands forever, unlike the changing human heart and the fading glory of the world. Help me to stop depending on what is passing and to root my heart in Your word every day. When I am weak, may You hold me in Your loving arms and lead me on the path You have prepared for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: You Are Not Alone, for God Himself Goes with You
v: Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said to them, “I am one hundred twenty years old today. I can no more go out and come in. The LORD has said to me, ‘You shall not go over this Jordan.’
The LORD your God himself will go over before you. He will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess them. Joshua will go over before you, as the LORD has spoken.
The LORD will do to them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
The LORD will deliver them up before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment which I have commanded you.
Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them, for the LORD your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”

Moses called to Joshua, and said to him in the sight of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you shall go with this people into the land which the LORD has sworn to their fathers to give them; and you shall cause them to inherit it.
The LORD himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.”
b: These are Moses’ words of encouragement to the people and to Joshua near the end of his life, and they are the deepest source of comfort and strength for God’s people in times of change. Although Moses could not enter the Promised Land, he put the emphasis on the presence of God, so that the people would understand that the true leader is not any person, but God himself.

When people face the unknown, a new responsibility, or a new season, the feelings that come most often are unease and fear. But God’s word is clear: you do not go forward alone, for Yahweh your God himself goes with you. He will not fail you or forsake you.

This is a call to live in faithfulness and to move forward by faith. It does not depend on human experience or resources, but on the God who opens the way and goes before you. You do not need to wait until everything is ready before you take a step. What you need is to believe his promise.
a: Learn to depend on God’s presence in times of change
Whether it is a new stage of life, a job change, or a shift in relationships, remember that God is your steady support.
Choose to be strong and courageous when you face difficulty
Being strong does not mean suppressing fear. It means firmly knowing that God goes with you, and not letting fear decide your direction.
Remember that God himself guides you as you take up your calling
Like Joshua, you and I have been called to take part in his plan. Do not shrink back because of your weakness; God will accomplish what he has promised.
q: When I face a challenge, do I let fear take control, or do I trust God by faith? Do I truly believe that he will not fail me or forsake me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You never fail me or forsake me. When I feel powerless and uncertain, help me to be strong and courageous, trusting You to lead before me, support beside me, and protect behind me. May I walk in Your way all my life, without fear, trusting You alone. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Not Only Hearers but Doers of the Word: Let Your Life Bear Real Fruit
v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;
for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.
But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.
If anyone among you thinks himself to be religious while he doesn’t bridle his tongue, but deceives his heart, this man’s religion is worthless.
Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
b: This passage is a very practical reminder about faith. James does not deal in theory. He points straight to the fact that real faith is not a slogan but a practice. It is not about how many sermons we have heard, but about letting God’s word bear fruit in our daily lives.

“Swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger” reflects an attitude of humility and teachability. True listening receives God’s word with a gentle heart. It is not in a hurry to voice its own opinions, nor does it use anger to defend its own righteousness.

But what matters more is this: “Be doers of the word, and not only hearers.” If we only hear and do not live it out, it is no more than glancing at a mirror and changing nothing. God’s word is not given for us to evaluate, but for us to live by, to be changed by, and to bear witness to.

A life that truly belongs to God is transformed from the inside out, and faith extends into action. Such a life produces three fruits: a disciplined tongue, practical care (such as looking after orphans and widows), and a pure life set apart from the world.
a: Cultivate a humble attitude toward the word, not rushing to speak or to anger
God’s word is not given to arm us for arguments, but to shape and renew us.
Put one thing you have heard into practice each day
Do not let the word become head knowledge. Let it become action by hands and feet, living out God’s heart.
Live out a pure life and genuine love in the details
Not outward piety, but a controlled tongue, a compassionate heart, and a clean life.
q: How much of the word have I heard, and how much have I done? Is my faith an accumulation of knowledge, or an act of obedience?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving Your word, like a seed that sprouts and grows in my heart. Help me not only to hear the word but to do it, not only to be moved but to respond. Let the light of Your word shine in my everyday life, so that I may be a child who pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Come Out of the Darkness and Live a Life of Light
v: For you were once darkness, but are now light in the Lord. Walk as children of light,
for the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth,
proving what is well pleasing to the Lord.
Have no fellowship with the unfruitful deeds of darkness, but rather even reprove them.
For it is a shame even to speak of the things which are done by them in secret.
But all things, when they are reproved, are revealed by the light, for everything that reveals is light.
Therefore he says, “Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”
Therefore watch carefully how you walk, not as unwise, but as wise,
b: In this passage Paul gives believers a startling reminder: you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. This is not only about behavior. It is about the transformation of our whole life. We have been rescued from sin and the power of darkness and now belong to Christ, so we should live in a way that matches our new identity.

Children of light bear the fruit of light, which is goodness, righteousness, and truth. These are not put-on behaviors, but a character that flows naturally once the Lord’s light has shone on us. When our hearts are open to God, the light comes in and our lives are changed.

Paul urges us not only to leave the deeds of darkness, but also to actively discern what pleases God. This is a kind of “spiritual awakening,” like waking from sleep and rising from the dead. The light of Christ not only lights our path but also renews our hearts, so that we no longer drift along like fools, but walk each step with wisdom.
a: Examine yourself daily: am I living in the light or in the dark?
Not by outward piety, but by letting God’s word shine on the motives and choices deep in our hearts.
Refuse to walk with darkness and choose the company of light
Not only staying away from sin, but standing boldly for truth, without compromise and without silence.
Choose wisdom and alertness in everyday life
In our words, time, money, and relationships, live with the wisdom and witness that please God.
q: Am I really living in the light? Is the fruit of my life goodness and truthfulness, or compromise and self?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that through Jesus Christ You called me out of darkness to be a child of light. Help me to live in Your light every day, to bear the fruit of goodness, righteousness, and truth, and to walk wisely on the path You have prepared for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Let Justice and Mercy Be the Foundation of Your Life
v: The LORD said, “Go down to the house of the king of Judah, and speak this word there:
‘Hear the LORD’s word, king of Judah, who sits on David’s throne—you, your servants, and your people who enter in by these gates.

The LORD says: “Execute justice and righteousness, and deliver him who is robbed out of the hand of the oppressor. Do no wrong. Do no violence to the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow. Don’t shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you do this thing indeed, then kings sitting on David’s throne will enter in by the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses—they, their servants, and their people.
But if you will not hear these words, I swear by myself,” says the LORD, “that this house will become a desolation.”’”
b: This is a direct call from Yahweh through the prophet Jeremiah to the king of Judah, and a reminder to every leader and everyone who lives under authority: fearing God is not only worshiping in the temple, but practicing justice and righteousness in daily life.

God cares not only about a nation’s sacrifices and rituals, but also about whether anyone in the city is being oppressed, whether innocent blood is being shed, and whether people see the fatherless and the widow and look the other way. Justice and mercy are not merely requirements of a system. They are the shape of life that belongs to God’s people.

God’s promise is clear: if they obey his word, the nation will be secure and the blessing of David’s throne will continue. But if they disobey, then despite its history and splendor, the city will become a desolation. This was a warning to the king of that day, and it is also a mirror for our lives.

God’s divine order is built on God’s justice and loving-kindness. If we center on ourselves, neglect the weak, and grow cold and unfeeling, we are heading toward desolation. But if, under authority, we are willing to act in the fear of God, even ordinary people can become channels of blessing.
a: Practice justice and mercy in everyday life
From the way you speak, to how you treat the vulnerable, to how you respond to injustice, every step is an act of fearing God.
Do not separate worship from action
Worshiping God is not only singing and praying, but living out God’s heart in daily life.
Choose the right foundation, and the blessing will be secure
Do not build on power, reputation, or achievement. Build your life and family on justice and honesty.
q: Do I care about what God cares about? Is my way of life aimed at his justice and mercy?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, make me a person who does justice, loves mercy, and walks humbly with You. Do not let me worship You only on the surface while turning away from Your heart in how I live. May my life before You be more than a godly appearance, and bear honest action and the fruit of mercy. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Remember the Lord’s Body and Blood, and Live a Life Covenanted to Him
v: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks for it, and broke it. He gave to the disciples and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”
He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave to them, saying, “All of you drink it,
for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins.
But I tell you that I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”
b: On the last night before his suffering, Jesus shared the Passover meal with his disciples, and turned that meal into a turning point in the history of redemption for all humanity. He took the bread and said, “This is my body,” and took the cup and said, “This is my blood of the new covenant,” opening for the disciples, and for us, a road to forgiveness and new life.

This was no ordinary meal, but a sacred covenant. With his own body and blood, Jesus replaced the sacrificial system of the old covenant and established for us a new covenant, an everlasting covenant founded on his sacrifice and centered on forgiveness and love.

Each time we observe the Lord’s Supper and reflect on this passage, we are not only remembering the Lord’s suffering, but also reminding ourselves: Am I living in this covenant relationship? Do I take the Lord’s life as my standard and adjust my choices and direction by it? The Lord laid down his life for me. Am I willing to live for him?

Jesus also left us a hope: “I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until…” This means he will come again and gather with us in the Father’s Kingdom. This is our greatest motivation to endure, trust, and obey in this life, because the Lord has prepared an eternal banquet for us.
a: Regularly examine whether you are still living in the new covenant the Lord made
Not merely joining an outward ritual, but truly living out reverence and obedience toward the Lord.
Remember the Lord’s body and blood with a thankful heart
Each time you think of the Lord’s sacrifice, let it make you more humble, more loving toward the Lord, and more willing to forgive others.
Treat every day as a chance to walk with the Lord
The Lord shed his blood for me. Does what I do today bring him glory?
q: Am I living a life covenanted to the Lord? The Lord laid down his life for me. Am I willing to lay myself down for him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that through Jesus You gave body and blood for me and made an unchanging covenant with me. Keep in me a heart of reverence and gratitude, that I may remember the Lord’s sacrifice every day, and live a life worthy of the covenant with Him, pleasing to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Position Is Temporary; the Fear of God Is the True Foundation
v: “‘However, I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, but I will make him prince all the days of his life for David my servant’s sake whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes,
but I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand and will give it to you, even ten tribes.
I will give one tribe to his son, that David my servant may have a lamp always before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen for myself to put my name there.
I will take you, and you shall reign according to all that your soul desires, and shall be king over Israel.

It shall be, if you will listen to all that I command you, and will walk in my ways, and do that which is right in my eyes, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did, that I will be with you, and will build you a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel to you.
I will afflict the offspring of David for this, but not forever.’”
He made houses of high places, and made priests from among all the people, who were not of the sons of Levi.

Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast that is in Judah, and he went up to the altar. He did so in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he had made, and he placed in Bethel the priests of the high places that he had made.
b: This passage describes the turning point at which Israel was divided. Because Solomon turned away from him in his later years, God decided to split the kingdom, yet because of the covenant with David he kept one tribe for Solomon’s son. At the same time, God extended a gracious invitation to Jeroboam: “If you will walk in my ways, I will be with you and build you a sure house.”

But although Jeroboam was chosen, he did not respond to God’s heart. As soon as he took the throne he fell into fear and scheming. He did not want the people to go back to Jerusalem to worship, for fear of losing power, so he set up golden calves, established a new system of worship, and even appointed priests who did not belong to God. Every step he took led him further from the God who had given him the opportunity.

This reminds us that God can raise a person up, and he can also let a person bring about his own ruin. The authority and grace God gives are not for fulfilling our own desires, but for accomplishing his purpose. If we fear God as David did, we will still receive grace even when we stumble; but if, like Jeroboam, we center on ourselves, it will lead in the end to the ruin of a whole family and kingdom.
a: The position and opportunity God gives are for accomplishing his purpose
What we have is not for protecting ourselves, but for carrying out God’s plan.
Do not replace God’s heart with human methods
Even if the motive seems reasonable, anything that departs from God’s standard will in the end bring ruin and judgment.
The fear of God is the foundation of a secure life
Not having resources or power, but being willing to act according to God’s heart.
q: Am I faithful and reverent in the position God has given me? When I face a choice, do I obey God, or protect myself in human ways?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for arranging every step of my life, whether in high position or in ordinary days, as a trust from You. Keep me from straying from Your heart out of fear or selfish desire. Teach me to fear You and to do what is right in Your eyes, so that my life stands on a firm foundation and becomes a witness to Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Boldness Does Not Come From Ourselves but From Being With Jesus
v: As they spoke to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came to them,
being upset because they taught the people and proclaimed in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
In the morning, their rulers, elders, and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem.
Annas the high priest was there, with Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and as many as were relatives of the high priest.
When they had stood Peter and John in the middle of them, they inquired, “By what power, or in what name, have you done this?”
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “You rulers of the people and elders of Israel,
if we are examined today concerning a good deed done to a crippled man, by what means this man has been healed,

may it be known to you all, and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, this man stands here before you whole in him.
He is ‘the stone which was regarded as worthless by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner.’
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven that is given among men, by which we must be saved!”
Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and had perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marveled. They recognized that they had been with Jesus.
b: Peter and John healed a lame beggar at the temple, and this shook the religious leaders. They were questioned and surrounded, standing before the most powerful religious and political figures of their day. By ordinary reasoning, two common men with no background and no status should have shrunk back, yet they showed great boldness and bore firm witness to Jesus.

Where did this boldness come from? Not from self-confidence, eloquence, or strategy, but from the fact that “they had been with Jesus.” This sentence reveals the true source of spiritual authority: a relationship with Jesus. It is not position that makes a person strong, but being filled with the Holy Spirit, knowing whom you have believed, and knowing that the risen Jesus still reigns.

Peter’s message was clear and direct: “There is salvation in no one else.” This is not narrow-mindedness, but firmness of faith. When we are sure that Jesus is the only Savior, we will not be shaken by opposing voices.

In this age of many “truths” and confused values, God calls us back to the simplest source: walking with Jesus. Not through outward equipment, but through connection with him, we live out a witness that is fearless and uncompromising.
a: Practice walking closely with Jesus every day
Don’t just know about Jesus. Let him be your daily presence and your support.
Hold on to the truth under pressure and questioning
Do not water down the truth to please people, and do not compromise your faith for safety.
Let your life be recognized as that of someone who has been with Jesus
Not through slogans, but through living out love, truth, and strength, so that people see the image of the Lord.
q: Does my life show people that I am a disciple of Jesus? Am I willing to keep proclaiming Jesus’ name even amid opposition?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for letting me know Jesus Christ, so that I can be strong in weakness and still have hope in hardship. Fill me with the Holy Spirit, that I may have courage to face persecution and challenge, and to witness for Jesus rather than defend myself. May my life be a sign of Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Ten Commandments Are Not Restrictions but Boundaries of Freedom Within Love
v: God spoke all these words, saying,
“Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
You shall labor six days, and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;
for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day; therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.
“Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.
“You shall not murder.
“You shall not commit adultery.
“You shall not steal.
“You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
“You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
b: This passage is the latter part of the Ten Commandments that God himself gave to Israel. It covers relationships between people and is a blueprint for God’s people to live out the values of the Kingdom on earth.

Many think of commandments as restrictions, but they are in fact boundaries of love, a path God set up to protect us so that we can live in true freedom and peace in our relationships, our daily lives, and our hearts. When we no longer covet, no longer deceive, and no longer destroy relationships, we are truly able to live out the dignity of being made in God’s image.
The Sabbath reminds us that our worth does not come from endless toil, but from being willing to lay things down and rest in God’s presence. We are God’s children, not slaves of the world.
When honoring parents is made a commandment, we see how much God values the family. This is the most basic order between people, and the starting point for learning respect, gratitude, and obedience.

God’s law is not only a requirement for behavior, but also a requirement for the heart. “You shall not covet” is discipline for the desires of the heart; “You shall not give false testimony” builds the character of honesty. Every commandment is meant to make us more like him and to live in his likeness.
a: Treat the commandments as God’s love and protection for you
Don’t see them only as duties, but as boundaries drawn for the blessing of your life.
Set aside time each week to keep the Sabbath
In a fast-paced world, learn to stop, not because there is nothing to do, but to remember who your true source is.
Live a witness each day of not coveting, not oppressing, and not harming
Not merely avoiding mistakes, but actively building healthy, righteous, loving relationships.
q: Do I value God’s commandments or neglect them? What areas of my life need to be aligned and renewed by God’s word once again?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving the commandments and teaching me how to live a life that pleases You. Help me not only to know them but to be willing to obey, so that my relationships, my daily life, and my thoughts are pruned and built up by Your word. May I live not only in freedom but in a way that delights You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When You Cannot See Jesus, He Still Walks With You
v: Behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
They talked with each other about all of these things which had happened.
While they talked and questioned together, Jesus himself came near, and went with them.
But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
He said to them, “Foolish people, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”
Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
They came near to the village where they were going, and he acted like he would go further.
They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.” He went in to stay with them.
When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.
Their eyes were opened and they recognized him; then he vanished out of their sight.
They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”
They rose up that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”
They related the things that happened along the way, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.
b: This passage records how, after his resurrection, Jesus appeared to two discouraged and disappointed disciples. They were walking a road of disappointment, leaving Jerusalem, moving from the center of hope toward the edge of despair. They were talking about their loss, their confusion, and their unfulfilled expectations.
But Jesus himself came near and walked with them, though their eyes were kept from recognizing him. This reminds us that even when we cannot see the Lord in our low places, he is still with us.

Jesus did not reveal who he was right away. He began by explaining the Scriptures, and their hearts were set on fire again. When they invited him to stay, Jesus opened their eyes in the breaking of the bread, and they saw him. That breaking of bread was more than an action. It was a restart of love and truth that turned their faith around from its low point.

One encounter with the risen Lord changed the whole direction of these two lives. They had been on the road going away, and now they immediately turned and went back on the road of witness. This is the effect of walking with the Lord: hearts set on fire, eyes opened, and steps turned around.
a: In disappointment or confusion, remember the Lord is still walking beside you
Even if you cannot feel it, his presence has never left.
Let God’s word rekindle your cold heart
Return to Scripture every day and let truth renew your faith and hope.
Invite Jesus into your life and your everyday days
Like those two disciples, say, “Stay with us, Lord.”
q: Am I on a road of disappointment right now? Am I willing to invite Jesus again into my heart and into my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that even when I cannot see You, You still walk with me. Open my spiritual eyes so that disappointment does not blind me, and I may recognize Your presence again. May Your word rekindle the fire in my heart, so that I turn back with courage and bear witness for You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Trust God’s Provision, and You Will Experience Grace That Never Runs Out
v: After a while, the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.
The LORD’s word came to him, saying,
“Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to sustain you.”

So he arose and went to Zarephath; and when he came to the gate of the city, behold, a widow was there gathering sticks. He called to her and said, “Please get me a little water in a jar, that I may drink.”
As she was going to get it, he called to her and said, “Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand.”

She said, “As the LORD your God lives, I don’t have anything baked, but only a handful of meal in a jar and a little oil in a jar. Behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and bake it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.”
Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go and do as you have said; but make me a little cake from it first, and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for you and for your son.
For the LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘The jar of meal will not run out, and the jar of oil will not fail, until the day that the LORD sends rain on the earth.’”
She went and did according to the saying of Elijah; and she, he, and her household ate many days.
The jar of meal didn’t run out and the jar of oil didn’t fail, according to the LORD’s word, which he spoke by Elijah.
b: This passage takes place during a great famine in Israel. Elijah had been sustained by the brook and the ravens, but then the brook dried up. In human eyes it was a moment when everything had run out, yet it was the beginning of God’s intervention. God sent him to Zarephath to find an extremely poor widow, someone who seemed to have no means at all, and she became the one God chose to provide for him.

When Elijah asked her for water and bread, she told him honestly about her poverty and despair, but Elijah answered, “Don’t be afraid.” God’s word came to this woman and gave her a choice of faith: first make a cake for the servant of God, then for herself and her son. This was not an unreasonable request, but a call to faith.

Her obedience brought God’s supernatural provision: the jar of meal did not run out and the jar of oil did not fail. God did not provide once for all. He provided daily, steadily, continuously. It was not an overflowing barn, but enough for each day, just what was needed, so that people would depend on him each day and come to know him.

This passage teaches us that in times of lack, choosing to trust God and putting his word first is the beginning of experiencing his faithful provision. God delights to do great things through small faith.
a: Keep responding to God’s word even in hard times
Even when conditions are not ideal, God asks us to believe first and act first, and then he shows his faithfulness.
Don’t despise the little meal and oil in your hand
God does not look at how much you have, but at whether you are willing to give it. He can use something small to do wonders.
Learn to depend on God’s daily provision
God may not give you everything at once, but he will give you enough grace for each day.
q: When I feel lack and hardship, do I fear what I see, or do I respond to God’s word in faith? Am I willing to give to the Lord first and trust his provision?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I face difficulty and shortage, give me faith like the widow of Zarephath, willing to obey Your word and to give myself to You first. Help me believe that Your daily provision never ends, so that I learn to trust You in lack and experience You in obedience. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Turning Back and Remembering: The Starting Point for Rebuilding Faith and Life
v: Now in the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel were assembled with fasting, with sackcloth, and dirt on them.
The offspring of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners and stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
“You also came down on Mount Sinai, and spoke with them from heaven, and gave them right ordinances and true laws, good statutes and commandments,
and made known to them your holy Sabbath, and commanded them commandments, statutes, and a law, by Moses your servant,

and gave them bread from the sky for their hunger, and brought water out of the rock for them for their thirst, and commanded them that they should go in to possess the land which you had sworn to give them.
“But they and our fathers behaved proudly, hardened their neck, didn’t listen to your commandments,

and refused to obey. They weren’t mindful of your wonders that you did among them, but hardened their neck, and in their rebellion appointed a captain to return to their bondage. But you are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake them.
b: “But you are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake them. 18 Even when they had made a molten calf and said, ‘This is your God who brought you up out of Egypt,’ and had committed awful blasphemies, 19 yet you in your manifold mercies didn’t forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud didn’t depart from over them by day, to lead them in the way, neither the pillar of fire by night, to show them light, and the way in which they should go. 20 You gave your good Spirit to instruct them, and didn’t withhold your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst. 21 Yes, forty years you sustained them in the wilderness, and they lacked nothing. Their clothes didn’t grow old, and their feet didn’t swell.”

This account comes after Nehemiah led the people in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, when everyone gathered before God in a great assembly of repentance. They wore sackcloth, fasted, and put dust on their heads. This was not a religious ritual but real repentance. They confessed their own sins and those of their ancestors, admitting that their failure came not from circumstances but from leaving God’s word.

Yet the declaration that follows their repentance is not full of condemnation. It remembers how God showed grace again and again through history. He gave the law, led them out of Egypt, and met their needs in the wilderness. Even when they rebelled by making the golden calf and hardening their necks, he still showed great mercy and did not leave them or forsake them.

This reminds us that turning back is not only admitting our mistakes, but also remembering God’s faithfulness and love. God knows human weakness. He does not wait for us to be perfect; he waits for us to be willing to come back. He is willing to teach, provide, forgive, and guide us, so that we can walk the right path again.

For us, the first step in rebuilding a life is not changing our circumstances, but remembering God in our hearts, fearing him, and obeying his leading. This is the foundation of a life that belongs to God.
a: True repentance includes confessing and remembering
Admit your own offenses, and also remember how God led and forgave you in the past.
Remember God’s past grace in hard times
When you cannot see a way out now, recall how he guided, provided for, and forgave you before.
Trust God’s presence and continued provision
God kept clothes from wearing out and feet from swelling for forty years. Today he can also provide all you need on your wilderness road.
q: Am I willing to truly admit my rebellion? Do I remember how God forgave, guided, and provided for me in the past?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I confess that I have gone my own way and forgotten Your grace. But today I turn to You and remember Your faithful love and continued provision. Forgive me, and lead me back to the path You have prepared for me, so that in reverence and obedience I may rebuild a life that belongs to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When God Arises, Troubles Flee, and He Prepares a Path of Abundance for His People
v: Let God arise! Let his enemies be scattered! Let them who hate him also flee before him.
As smoke is driven away, so drive them away. As wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
But let the righteous be glad. Let them rejoice before God. Yes, let them rejoice with gladness.
Sing to God! Sing praises to his name! Extol him who rides on the clouds: to the LORD, his name! Rejoice before him!
A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
God sets the lonely in families. He brings out the prisoners with singing, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.
God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wilderness... Selah.
The earth trembled. The sky also poured down rain at the presence of the God of Sinai— at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
You, God, sent a plentiful rain. You confirmed your inheritance when it was weary.
Your congregation lived therein. You, God, prepared your goodness for the poor.
b: This is a psalm of David proclaiming God’s sovereignty and grace. It begins with the declaration, “Let God arise!” When God steps in, our situation changes, enemies retreat, and troubles are like smoke and wax, with nowhere to hide in his presence. God is not a passive observer, but a God who vindicates the righteous and stands up for the wronged.

He is not only a mighty conqueror of enemies, but also a father to the fatherless and a defender of widows, which shows that his love is both gentle and firm. He not only drives back the wicked, but also personally cares for the least, giving the lonely a place to belong and setting the captive heart free. This is the God we believe in: almighty and loving together, with justice and grace side by side.

When God led his people out of Egypt, he not only marched before them in the wilderness, but also sent plentiful rain to refresh the dry land and provide for them in their weariness. Today we too walk our own wilderness roads, perhaps pressure, loss, illness, or family challenges, but God is still the Lord who prepares his goodness for the poor.
His promise is this: when he arises, whether you are lonely, imprisoned, or weary, he will open a way for you, send the rain of his grace, and let you dwell in the land of his goodness.
a: In hard times, call on God to arise and bring reversal and release
Not by your own struggle, but by inviting God to step in himself.
Remember that God’s heart is for the lonely, the poor, and the wronged
Do not think you are too small or too weak. God is watching over you and will give you freedom and a home.
Believe in weariness that God will still send the rain
He knows how tired you are. His grace will not be late; it will come just on time.
q: Am I willing to let God “arise” in my life? Am I willing to believe he can send the rain of grace on my dry ground?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I feel weary, lonely, and trapped, I call on You to arise. Drive back my enemies and set my heart free. You are the Father of the fatherless and a God of mercy. May You reign in my life and send down upon me the rain of grace from heaven. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Follow in Jesus’ Footsteps on the Path of Self-Giving and Healing
v: For you were called to this, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example, that you should follow his steps,
who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.”
When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.
For you were going astray like sheep; but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
b: In this passage Peter deeply portrays the suffering Christ endured for us, not only to accomplish salvation, but also to leave an example for our lives, a path we can follow. Jesus did not only teach us how to live. He personally walked the road of self-giving, so that we could learn from his steps and follow them.

He did not sin and no deceit was found in his mouth, yet he willingly suffered for sinners. Facing insult and persecution, he did not answer back or take revenge, but entrusted everything to the Father who judges righteously. This was deep trust and humility, and it showed a calm and victory that rose above circumstances.

Jesus did not only bear our sins. He also set us free from the bondage of sin so that we can “live to righteousness.” This is not only forgiveness of life, but a change of direction. We no longer live for ourselves, but for the Lord who loved us and gave his life for us.

“By his stripes you were healed.” This is not only a promise of bodily healing, but also the restoration of what is broken deep within the soul. Only when we return to Jesus, the Shepherd and Overseer, are our lives truly watched over, guided, and repaired.
a: When misunderstood or wronged, learn to commit yourself to God
Don’t rush to defend yourself. God is the Lord who judges righteously.
Let Jesus’ suffering be the strength for you to do right
He suffered for you not so that you would fear, but so that you can live boldly for righteousness.
Walk in the Lord’s footsteps each day
Not by your own good deeds, but by learning his character and heart step by step through faith.
q: Am I willing to follow Jesus’ footsteps and choose obedience and trust in hard times? Am I letting his stripes heal the broken places in my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus to suffer for me. He not only atoned for my sin but also left me an example. Help me, when I face challenges, to learn his patience and trust, so that by his stripes I am healed and I live out his righteousness and love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Since We Are God’s Children, Let Us Purify Ourselves as the Lord Is Pure
v: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.
Beloved, now we are children of God. It is not yet revealed what we will be; but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is.
Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure.
Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness.
You know that he was revealed to take away our sins, and no sin is in him.
Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin. Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him.
b: This passage opens with a beautiful declaration: “See what great love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God!” Becoming God’s children is not something we deserve, but comes from his love, which he showed first. It is a grace of identity, and also a spiritual calling.

When we become God’s children, our lives no longer follow the old patterns. Though we still live on earth, our hope is the day we will see the Lord face to face, when “we will be like him” because we will see him as he is. This hope does not make us idle. It urges us to “purify ourselves, even as he is pure.”

This purifying is not only outward behavior but inward renewal. Those who truly remain in him do not keep living in sin, because we have turned to the one who takes away sin. If a person still deliberately lives in sin and does not care about holiness, it shows he has not yet truly known the Lord.

To be God’s child is both an identity and a responsibility. We do not do right in order to be saved. Because we are already saved and received as God’s children, we are willing to purify ourselves and live like him.
a: Remind yourself every day
“I am a child of God.” Do not let the voices of the world define you, but let God’s love shape your identity and your worth.
Live each day with the goal of seeing the Lord
We do not live for fleeting success in this life, but prepare for an eternal meeting.
Choose to connect with the Lord when sin tempts you, and do not let sin reign
Not by willpower, but by remaining in him and living out victory and purity.
q: Am I living the way a child of God should? Do I truly long to be made pure like Jesus?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for Your wonderful love that lets me be Your child. Help me not only to know this identity but to be willing to live it out in a way worthy of You. Purify me, make me more like Jesus every day, and prepare me for the day I will see You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When Worship Becomes the Center of Life, We See the True Throne
v: After these things I looked and saw a door opened in heaven; and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, was one saying, “Come up here, and I will show you the things which must happen after this.”
Immediately I was in the Spirit. Behold, there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne
that looked like a jasper stone and a sardius. There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald to look at.
Around the throne were twenty-four thrones. On the thrones were twenty-four elders sitting, dressed in white garments, with crowns of gold on their heads.
Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal. In the middle of the throne, and around the throne were four living creatures full of eyes before and behind.
The first creature was like a lion, the second creature like a calf, the third creature had a face like a man, and the fourth was like a flying eagle.

The four living creatures, each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within. They have no rest day and night, saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!”
b: “Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come.”

9 Whenever the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to him who sits on the throne, to him who lives forever and ever, 10 the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne and worship him who lives forever and ever, and throw their crowns before the throne, saying, 11 “Worthy are you, our Lord and our God, to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, for you created all things, and because of your will they existed, and were created.”

This passage opens a scene in heaven. It is where the apostle John begins to receive his vision, and it reveals the heart of worship that runs through the whole book of Revelation. When the door of heaven opens, the true throne is unveiled—not a human seat of power, not an earthly government, but the Lord of eternity who created all things and rules over history.

The focus of the whole heavenly court is not who holds power or what will happen next, but God, “the one sitting on the throne.” He shines in glory like jasper and sardius, and a rainbow surrounds him, a sign of love and faithfulness within glory. The four living creatures worship day and night, and the twenty-four elders fall down and gladly lay down their crowns. It is a picture of worship that never ceases and glory that never stops flowing.

This reminds us that when our hearts are drawn to earthly thrones—money, achievement, power, reputation—the true throne is in heaven, and true authority is in God’s hands. Worship is not just a Sunday ritual. It is laying down our crowns, our right to rule, and our very lives before God, every day.

This is how a life that belongs to God is trained: surrender authority to the One who sits on the throne, turn your focus to the God who created all things and is worthy of glory, and let worship be more than songs on your lips—let it be the posture of your whole life.
a: Begin each day with worship, refocusing on God as the Lord who sits on the throne
In the middle of busyness and chaos, let the throne in heaven be the anchor of your heart.
Lay down your own “crown” and let God be King
Do not clutch your own plans, achievements, and control. Hand them over to God’s rule.
Learn to answer every everyday call with worship
Not only at gatherings, but at home, at work, in hardship and in blessing, worship him in all of it.
q: Am I still chasing earthly thrones? Am I willing to lay down my crown and let God truly be King in my life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for letting me see the throne in heaven and understand that You are the Lord who reigns. I give my authority to You and lay my crown before You. May my life honor You as King every day. Teach me the worship of heaven, and help me to honor You on earth as it is in heaven. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Run the Heavenly Race with Your Eyes Fixed on Jesus
v: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.
b: Here the author compares our walk of faith to a long-distance race—not a sprint, but a test of endurance. Along the way a cloud of witnesses surrounds us, encouraging us and reminding us that this road is not run in vain. But what truly lets us run well and not grow weary is “looking to Jesus.”

Jesus is both the author and the perfecter of faith. We were able to begin this race because of his salvation, and we are able to finish because of his presence and power. He himself ran the road to the cross; because he saw the joy set before him, he despised the shame and endured the suffering, and now he sits at the right hand of the throne.

This reminds us that if we look only at the difficulties in front of us, we grow weary and discouraged; but if we turn our eyes to Jesus, we are strengthened again. True faith keeps its focus in the middle of the storm, fixing our eyes on Jesus and not letting burdens and sin drag us back.

Faith is not based on feelings but on trust. We live not by our own strength but by looking to the life of Jesus. Whenever you want to give up or stop, think of the Lord who endured the cross and won the victory for you.
a: Practice “laying aside” every day
Lay aside burdens (like worry and fear) and throw off sin (like pride and self-pity), so you can run with a light heart.
Whatever the circumstances, turn your focus back to Jesus
He is not just waiting at the finish line. He runs beside you all the way.
Persevere with patience and faith
God’s road does not value short bursts of speed but faithfulness and lasting trust.
q: Am I carrying burdens or sin right now that keep me from running? Have I put my focus in the wrong place instead of fixing my eyes on Jesus?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for opening the way of faith through Jesus and for being willing to run beside me to the end. Help me lay aside my burdens and throw off what entangles me, so that each day I look to Jesus and do not lose my way in hard times. May I run this heavenly race not in my own strength, but by Your grace alone. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When God’s Love Fills the Heart, a Life of Loving One Another Flows Naturally
v: The multitude of those who believed were of one heart and soul. Not one of them claimed that anything of the things which he possessed was his own, but they had all things in common.
With great power, the apostles gave their testimony of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. Great grace was on them all.
For neither was there among them any who lacked, for as many as were owners of lands or houses sold them, and brought the proceeds of the things that were sold,
and laid them at the apostles’ feet; and distribution was made to each, according as anyone had need.
Joses, who by the apostles was also called Barnabas (which is, being interpreted, Son of Encouragement), a Levite, a man of Cyprus by race,
having a field, sold it and brought the money and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
b: This passage paints a beautiful picture of the early church: not a people with a perfect system or vast resources, but a community of believers thoroughly transformed by God’s love, living out “loving one another” with one heart.

When the power of Jesus’ resurrection was proclaimed through the apostles’ testimony, it was not only outward miracles that drew people, but the unity of life within that moved them. They were of one heart and soul. None of them looked at what they owned as “mine,” but gladly shared and supplied one another according to each one’s need.

This was not communism, and it was not forced giving. It was the natural overflow of a life that comes from believing in the Lord. A person who knows that everything comes from God no longer clutches possessions, but gladly lets them go to bless others.

The passage especially mentions a man named Barnabas. His original name was Joseph, but because he was always comforting and encouraging people, the apostles gave him a new name, Barnabas—“Son of Encouragement.” He is remembered not for some great deed but because he was willing to sell his field to bless the church, showing his love for the Lord and his care for people.
When a people let God’s love be King in their hearts, they will naturally give to one another and build one another up. This is exactly how the glory of God’s Kingdom is displayed on earth.
a: Learn to let go of the mindset of “mine” and live with a heart to share
A life that belongs to God is not about having more, but about being willing to give more.
Let the Lord’s love fill our thoughts and actions
The more we understand how much the Lord gave up for us, the more willing we are to give ourselves for others.
Become an “encourager” like Barnabas
Be a help and encouragement to others with your resources, your words, and your time.
q: Am I still holding tightly to the grace God has given me? Am I willing to let God use me to be a blessing to others?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for Your abundant grace that leaves me lacking nothing. Help me not to live only for myself, but to learn from the early church to put love into action, gladly sharing and building others up. May I become an outlet of Your love and live for Your glorious name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Put Your Hope in God, Not in the Hands of Men
v: Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD, my soul.
While I live, I will praise the LORD. I will sing praises to my God as long as I exist.
Don’t put your trust in princes, in a son of man in whom there is no help.
His spirit departs, and he returns to the earth. In that very day, his thoughts perish.
Happy is he who has the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the LORD, his God,
who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them; who keeps truth forever;
who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry. The LORD frees the prisoners.
The LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD raises up those who are bowed down. The LORD loves the righteous.
The LORD preserves the foreigners. He upholds the fatherless and widow, but he turns the way of the wicked upside down.
The LORD will reign forever; your God, O Zion, to all generations. Praise the LORD!
b: Psalm 146 is a song full of faith and worship, the first of the closing “Hallelujah” psalms. The psalmist begins, “Praise Yahweh, my soul!” It is a call to himself, a reminder that whatever the circumstances, he must turn his focus to God.

The psalmist not only means to “praise Yahweh while I live,” but also says, “I will sing praises to my God while I have any being.” Worship does not wait until everything goes smoothly. It treats every day as a chance to sing.

He then warns: “Don’t put your trust in princes, in a son of man,” because human life is limited and so is human ability. No matter how great the power or how deep the relationship, when the spirit departs, the body returns to the earth, and all its plans perish with it. Only the one whose hope is in “the God of Jacob” is happy, because he relies on the Lord who made heaven and earth, keeps truth, and does justice.

This God not only created the heavens and the earth, he also cares for people personally: he executes justice for the oppressed, gives food to the hungry, frees the prisoners, opens the eyes of the blind, raises up those who are bowed down, preserves the foreigner, and upholds the fatherless and the widow. He is not a distant God, but the God nearest to the afflicted.
And this God does not reign for a moment only, but is the Lord who rules “forever.” When we worship him, we set our hearts again on an authority that never changes.
a: Do not rely on human methods or resources; look to God alone
When you turn your focus from people back to God, you will truly experience heavenly peace and power.
Choose to worship and trust even in difficulty
Praise is not merely an emotional reaction, but a choice of faith.
Learn God’s heart and become a helper to the lonely and afflicted
Worshiping God also means living out his character and caring for everyone he loves.
q: Am I still placing my hope in human help, systems, or circumstances? Am I willing to trust wholeheartedly in the God who reigns forever?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, You are the Lord who made heaven and earth and rules over all. I no longer want to rely on people, nor let circumstances stir up my heart. Strengthen my faith, so that I worship You and look to You all my life. When I am disappointed, help me remember that You are the Savior who is faithful forever. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: God’s Grace Goes Beyond Bloodline and Past to Fulfill His Plan of Salvation
v: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.
Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.
Ram became the father of Amminadab. Amminadab became the father of Nahshon. Nahshon became the father of Salmon.
Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.
Jesse became the father of King David. David the king became the father of Solomon by her who had been Uriah’s wife.
After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud. Abiud became the father of Eliakim. Eliakim became the father of Azor.
Azor became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Achim. Achim became the father of Eliud.
Eliud became the father of Eleazar. Eleazar became the father of Matthan. Matthan became the father of Jacob.
Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.
b: This genealogy may look “dry,” but it hides a deep message of grace and redemption. Matthew begins by pointing out that Jesus is “the son of David, the son of Abraham”—not merely a historical placement, but the fulfillment of God’s promise. Jesus came to fulfill the promise God made to Abraham, “in you all the families of the earth will be blessed,” and the promise to David, “your throne shall be established forever.”

Yet this genealogy includes many scarred and broken people: Tamar, Rahab, and Ruth were all Gentile women; David fathered Solomon by the wife of Uriah, exposing David’s failure; and the descendants after Babylon were mostly exiles and forgotten names.
These people would never have been expected to enter the Messiah’s family line, yet God used these “imperfect” people to display his perfection and sovereignty.

This reminds us that God’s salvation does not select perfect people, but uses lives willing to be used by him. Even if you have a past, even if your background is ordinary, even if you have failed and fallen, God can still weave you into his plan and make you part of the continuing blessing.
a: Do not let your past deny God’s plan for you
He can turn the darkest history into the most glorious future.
Even as “one person in a generation,” you can be a vessel in God’s hands
Your faithfulness and trust will be remembered in God’s time.
Honor every spiritual inheritance and treasure your family line of faith
Whether you are a first-generation believer or a link in a long spiritual history, God will use you to carry his promise forward.
q: Am I still held back by my past? Do I believe God can accomplish his grace and blessing through my life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for showing me that You never despise a person’s past and are never limited by their failures. Use my humble life as You used Tamar, Ruth, and Solomon. Let me be a part of Your plan of blessing, live for You, and pass on Your grace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When You Are in a Desolate Place, God Is Right There with You
v: Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.
He came to a certain place, and stayed there all night, because the sun had set. He took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.
He dreamed and saw a stairway set upon the earth, and its top reached to heaven. Behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
Behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, “I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. I will give the land you lie on to you and to your offspring.

Your offspring will be as the dust of the earth, and you will spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. In you and in your offspring, all the families of the earth will be blessed.
Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.”
Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”
He was afraid, and said, “How awesome this place is! This is none other than God’s house, and this is the gate of heaven.”
b: This passage records a deeply significant turning point in Jacob’s life. Fleeing from his brother Esau, alone, with night falling, he had to sleep in the wilderness with a stone for a pillow. Yet it was at this loneliest, most anxious, most helpless moment that God personally appeared to him.

Jacob dreamed of a stairway connecting earth and heaven, with angels of God ascending and descending. This was no ordinary dream but a revelation from God. God’s presence is not limited by place. He can speak to us in the most desolate wilderness and make known his promises and plans.

God’s words to Jacob were not only a promise for the future but also for the present: “I am with you… I will not leave you.” These words became a new turning point in Jacob’s life. He awoke and said, “Surely Yahweh is in this place, and I didn’t know it.” Like Jacob, we often see only our problems in hard times and fail to realize God’s presence and work.

From this night on, Jacob came to know God not only as the God of his father Isaac and his grandfather Abraham, but as his own God. God entered his life with a vision and a promise, and changed his future.
a: Do not assume God is absent because your circumstances are desolate
God often speaks to you in your loneliest, most exhausted, most hopeless place.
Learn to notice God’s presence, even in ordinary days
Jacob was merely running from danger, yet God prepared a heavenly turning point right in the middle of it.
Let God’s promise be the basis of your next step of faith
Do not walk through life by what you see; step out in faith according to God’s word.
q: Like Jacob, have I overlooked God’s presence? In the moments I consider “God-less,” might God be quietly at work?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being with me even when I am lonely and helpless. Open my eyes to see Your presence and the path You have prepared for me. May I no longer judge my circumstances by feelings, but respond to Your call by faith. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: In Everything, Choose a Response of Goodness and Gratitude
v: See that no one returns evil for evil to anyone, but always follow after that which is good for one another and for all.
Always rejoice.
Pray without ceasing.
In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.
b: In this short but powerful passage, Paul points believers to three core attitudes of life: joy, prayer, and thanksgiving. This is not merely moral advice. It is “the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you,” an expression of a life that belongs to God.

First, we live in a world full of evil and injustice, where people easily answer harm with harm. But Paul says, “Always follow after that which is good,” not only toward fellow believers but toward everyone. When we are hurt, the most natural reaction is revenge, but God wants us to respond differently—to overcome evil with good and be peacemakers.

Next, he reminds us to “always rejoice.” This joy is not built on smooth circumstances or things going our way, but on the faith of walking with God and knowing he reigns. Even in suffering, because the Lord is with us, we can still rejoice.

“Pray without ceasing” does not mean our lips must move twenty-four hours a day. It means practicing a life attitude of staying connected to God at all times and entrusting everything to him. Such prayer keeps our spirits alert and strong, and keeps us from being swayed by the world.

Finally, “in everything give thanks” is the most distinctive mark of a Christian. We give thanks not only when everything is good but in everything, because we know God reigns and that every situation can become a vessel of growth and grace.
Such a life is one that lets Jesus be King and lets the Holy Spirit lead, a life that worships God in daily living and shows his glory.
a: Practice “overcoming evil with good” in conflict
Even when the other person is unfriendly, choose to respond with kindness and respect.
Let joy be the beginning and end of every day
Do not let emotions rule your day; adjust your mindset with faith and gratitude.
Build a rhythm of “living in prayer”
Not just morning and evening prayers, but entrusting every matter of the whole day to God and walking with him.
q: Am I easily swayed by circumstances and other people, losing my joy and gratitude? Am I willing to let God’s will be the standard of my daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for this good will You have given in Christ: that I rejoice, pray, and give thanks. Help me not to be provoked by evil or have my joy taken by circumstances, but to choose each day to live by relying on You and to live a life that glorifies You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: God Personally Shepherds His Sheep, Seeking the Lost and Healing the Wounded
v: “‘For the Lord GOD says: “Behold, I myself, even I, will search for my sheep, and will seek them out.

As a shepherd seeks out his flock in the day that he is among his sheep that are scattered abroad, so I will seek out my sheep. I will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day.

I will bring them out from the peoples, and gather them from the countries, and will bring them into their own land. I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the watercourses, and in all the inhabited places of the country.

I will feed them with good pasture, and their fold will be on the mountains of the height of Israel. There they will lie down in a good fold. They will feed on rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will cause them to lie down,” says the Lord GOD.

“I will seek that which was lost, and will bring back that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick; but I will destroy the fat and the strong. I will feed them in justice.”’
b: This passage is God’s tender yet sovereign word to the people of Israel. At that time, the leaders and shepherds had failed in their duty, causing God’s people to be scattered and to suffer, so God himself made a promise: he would become their shepherd and bring his flock back.

“I myself will search for my sheep”—this is a God of active love. He does not wait for the sheep to return but goes out to find them. His love is not a conditional waiting but a sacrificial going out, just like the Good Shepherd Jesus spoke of: “The Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

His shepherding is not form or system but real action: he leads the sheep home, brings them to places of rest, lets them lie down in safety, and feeds them in rich pasture. This is not only a figure of speech, but the real guidance God promises we can experience every day.

His love leans especially toward the wounded, the driven away, and the weak. He does not care only for the strong, but especially heals the broken, seeks the lost, binds up the wounds, and brings back the wanderers.
Such a shepherd is our God. When we are willing to let go of our own ways of “taking care of ourselves” and let him lead, provide, and restore, we enter true rest.
a: In confusion or loneliness, turn to God the Shepherd
Stop walking on your own; respond to his seeking and calling.
Let God’s word be your daily pasture and water
It is not enough to hear a little; come to his word every day and be satisfied.
Learn God’s way of shepherding and care for the lost and wounded
If we are his sheep, we should learn to shepherd the sheep he loves.
q: Am I still losing my way by my own methods? Am I willing to let God personally shepherd, restore, and lead my life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for not abandoning me, but personally seeking me, guiding me, and healing me. Shepherd my heart every day so I no longer wander, and teach me to be like You, seeking out, comforting, and supporting lost souls. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The New Heaven and New Earth Are Before Us, and God Himself Dwells with Man
v: I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.
I heard a loud voice out of heaven saying, “Behold, God’s dwelling is with people; and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God.
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.”
He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” He said, “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.”
One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls which were loaded with the seven last plagues came, and he spoke with me, saying, “Come here. I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.”
He carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God,
having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal;
b: This is the most glorious and ultimate picture in Revelation—God’s new creation, new city, and new presence. The New Jerusalem is not a religious center built by man, but a holy dwelling that comes “down out of heaven from God,” a new home God himself has prepared for his people.

The city is adorned like a bride, ready to meet the one she loves. God’s love is not distant or cold, but like the most tender waiting and welcoming of a wedding. We are not a group of strangers, but the Lord’s “bride,” who will be close to him forever.

God declares here, “Behold, God’s dwelling is with people.” He does not rule only from heaven, but desires to live personally with people. This is his heart, and the climax of the whole Bible—from the garden of Eden in Genesis, where man walked with God, to here, where man and God are never again separated.

The blessing here is not earthly prosperity but the deepest comfort of the heart: “He will wipe away every tear from their eyes.” Past wounds, brokenness, tears, death, pain, and loss are all wiped away, because “the first things have passed away.”

The city is filled with the glory of God, shining like a precious stone. This is not just visual beauty, but a display of holiness, dignity, and the presence of God. He makes all things new, so that every old failure and pain becomes past, and we enter a new glory and unity.
a: View the sufferings of this life with an eternal perspective
What God promises is not merely escape from pain, but everlasting comfort and healing to come.
Prepare yourself like a bride, adorned and waiting for the Lord’s return
Your daily choices, thoughts, and lifestyle are all preparing you for that day.
Live in “God’s presence,” not just waiting for the future but beginning now
Let God’s presence be your strength and hope every day.
q: Am I living like a bride with an eternal hope? Do I believe God is preparing for me a home with no tears and no pain?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for preparing the new heaven and new earth for me, and for promising to dwell with us and wipe away all our tears. Help me live each day in this glorious hope, and prepare myself in heart and action for the day of Your return. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: God Personally Watches Over His Flock and Gives True Joy and Satisfaction
v: “Hear the LORD’s word, you nations, and declare it in the distant islands. Say, ‘He who scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd does his flock.’
For the LORD has ransomed Jacob, and redeemed him from the hand of him who was stronger than he.

They will come and sing in the height of Zion, and will flow to the goodness of the LORD, to the grain, to the new wine, to the oil, and to the young of the flock and of the herd. Their soul will be as a watered garden. They will not sorrow any more at all.
Then the virgin will rejoice in the dance, the young men and the old together; for I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people will be satisfied with my goodness,” says the LORD.
b: This passage is a song of restoration God sings over Israel. After exile, scattering, and brokenness, God himself declares, “He who scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him.” This is not human effort but God’s own initiative in seeking and shepherding. He is the Good Shepherd who personally gathers the scattered sheep and brings them back into his arms.

God’s rescue does not merely pull people out of pain; it lets them experience his abundant goodness again. What he supplies is not only outward food (grain, new wine, oil), but a heart that is “like a watered garden”—full of life, full of joy, no longer dry and sorrowful.

When God personally reigns and shepherds, the sorrowful heart, the weary body, and the suppressed emotions are all transformed. He promises, “I will turn their mourning into joy… and make them rejoice from their sorrow.” This is not only a hope for the future but a renewal we can experience today.

He even cares for the priests who serve him—“I will satiate the soul of the priests with abundance”—showing that he values every faithful servant. The overall restoration and satisfaction do not come from outward systems or methods, but from grace that God himself pours out.
a: Believe that God is still the Shepherd who actively seeks and gathers us
Even if we once wandered far, he does not give up but personally calls us to return.
Let God’s goodness water the garden of our hearts
Be refreshed each day in his word and presence, and no longer leave yourself dry and sorrowful.
Become a vessel of joy and comfort to others
After you are healed and filled by God, share that heavenly joy and encouragement with others.
q: Is my heart like a watered garden, or is it still dry? Do I believe God can turn my sorrow and grief into joy and renew my strength?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the Shepherd of my life, willing to gather me, watch over me, and comfort me. Water my dry heart so that I find satisfaction and joy in Your goodness. However broken I have been, may You let me sing again today and become a witness of Your grace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
